method: Seven read-only auditors (A-G) each took a region of the specification (A-F) or the proto's REQUIRED fields (G) and recorded every RFC 2119 statement with the code and tests they opened. Their entries are model output: the ones this branch changed (changed_by) were re-verified by reproducing the defect and showing the new test fail without the fix; the rest are recorded as found and have not been independently re-verified. Notes and citations corrected to match the code without a change to it (2026-10-13) carry no changed_by: they were checked by reading the code, not by a failing test. Re-anchored 2026-10-14 from upstream main at 12e9d2fbb9ba, which the entries were made against, to the v1.0.1 tag: every spec_line, and every spec line number cited in a note, was moved through a line map built from the two texts by difflib (equal runs, and replaced blocks of equal length, map line for line); 191 entries moved, and the three §7.6.4 entries, whose text v1.0.1 does not have, moved to after_release.

entries.requirement: A generated JSON artifact (`spec/a2a.json`...) MAY be published for convenience to tooling and the website
entries.notes: Concerns the spec project's documentation build, not an SDK.

entries.requirement: SDK language bindings, schemas, and any other derived forms MUST be regenerated from the proto (directly or via code generation) rather than edited manually.
entries.notes: Every public serde type that mirrors a2a.proto is generated from it (ADR 0016, register R49): tools/a2a-codegen (protox, no protoc) writes crates/a2a-protocol-types/src/generated/ from the proto and codegen.toml, which records each deliberate difference with its reason and is refused when it names anything the proto lacks or omits a proto type. All 46 proto types and the PartContent enum are generated; the prost message types come from build.rs. CI's static checks run `a2a-codegen --check` (ci.yml:88), which fails when a generated file differs from what the proto makes (proven by the gate prover with a hand edit to generated/task.rs) and when any Rust file git knows of, outside src/generated/ and the generator, declares a struct, enum, union or type under one of the 47 generated names (shown 2026-10-15 by four injections: a struct in a tracked file, one in an untracked file, a type alias, a pub(crate) enum; each failed naming file and line). The vendored proto copies are checked byte-identical to the v1.0.1 release (check_proto_copies.sh, the two proto_schema_sync tests). The serde-prost conversions are hand-written code, not a derived form: each builds its target with a full struct literal (no `..Default::default()` in src/proto/convert/), so a field the proto adds to either generated side fails to compile until mapped. Not checked mechanically: that a hand-written conversion maps a field correctly, which the conversion round-trip tests and the proto_convert fuzz target cover.

entries.requirement: Migration guidance MUST be provided via an ancillary document when introducing major breaking changes.
entries.notes: Binds the specification maintainers.

entries.requirement: Legacy documentation anchors MUST be preserved (as hidden HTML anchors) to avoid breaking inbound links.
entries.notes: Binds the specification website.

entries.requirement: SDKs and JSON Schemas SHOULD provide deprecated alias types/definitions to maintain backward compatibility.
entries.notes: The two proto-deprecated OAuth flows (implicit, password) are kept so cards declaring them parse, and since 2026-10-11 carry #[deprecated] as the proto fields do. Two compile_fail doctests deny(deprecated) on each variant; removing the attribute makes the doctest compile and fail (shown). No v1.0 field was renamed, so no renamed-field aliases are needed.

entries.requirement: A deprecated name SHOULD NOT be removed earlier than the next major version after introduction of its replacement.
entries.notes: Both deprecated flows remain in the public enum and on the wire (wire_format_password_oauth_flow round-trips one); removal would be a semver-major change, which cargo-semver-checks gates in CI.

entries.requirement: The keywords "MUST", ... are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
entries.notes: Definitional.

entries.requirement: ContentTypeNotSupportedError: A Media Type provided in the request's message parts is not supported by the agent.
entries.notes: Only enforced when a card declares input modes and only for parts carrying an explicit mediaType; opt-out via allow_undeclared_input_modes.

entries.requirement: UnsupportedOperationError: Messages sent to Tasks that are in a terminal state ... cannot accept further messages.
TaskNotFoundError: The task ID does not exist or is not accessible.
The agent MAY create a new `Task` to process the provided message asynchronously
or MAY return a direct `Message` response for simple interactions.
entries.notes: Non-streaming only: Message returned when the executor emitted a message and nothing task-shaped (a task row is still persisted).

entries.requirement: The operation MUST return immediately with either task information or response message.
entries.notes: Read together with §3.2.2: with returnImmediately=true the Submitted snapshot is returned at once; the default (blocking) mode waits for terminal/interrupted state as §3.2.2 requires.

entries.requirement: Task processing MAY continue asynchronously after the response when a Task is returned.
entries.notes: Background event processor keeps persisting after the response.

entries.requirement: Subsequent events following a `Task` MAY include stream of TaskStatusUpdateEvent and TaskArtifactUpdateEvent objects
UnsupportedOperationError: Streaming is not supported by the agent
entries.notes: SendStreamingMessage against a card whose streaming capability is false or absent answers UnsupportedOperationError (-32004) over JSON-RPC (test added 2026-10-10, shown to fail with the check disabled). No-op when no card is configured; see §8.1 line 1970.

entries.requirement: UnsupportedOperationError: Messages sent to Tasks that are in a terminal state ... cannot accept further messages.
entries.notes: Shared code path with SendMessage (resolve_task_id runs before the streaming split); the test drives streaming=false only.

entries.requirement: ContentTypeNotSupportedError (streaming)
entries.notes: Same validate_send_params path as unary send.

entries.requirement: TaskNotFoundError (streaming)
entries.notes: Shared path; no streaming-specific test.

entries.requirement: The operation MUST establish a streaming connection for real-time updates.
entries.notes: All four bindings consume the same InMemoryQueueReader.

entries.requirement: The stream MUST follow one of these patterns: (1) Message-only stream ... (2) Task lifecycle stream
entries.notes: The executor's first event decides the pattern (InMemoryQueueReader::set_provisional_task): a Message makes a message-only stream, anything else a task stream that begins with the Task.

entries.requirement: Message-only stream: If the agent returns a Message, the stream MUST contain exactly one `Message` object and then close immediately.
entries.notes: Exactly one Message, then the reader returns None; a read dropped while waiting for the first event keeps the decision (cancel-safety test).

entries.requirement: Task lifecycle stream: If the agent returns a Task, the stream MUST begin with the Task object, followed by zero or more TaskStatusUpdateEvent or TaskArtifactUpdateEvent objects.
The stream MUST close when the task reaches a terminal state (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, REJECTED).
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-12 a reader ends once it has delivered a terminal state (and whatever was queued ahead of it), instead of waiting for the executor to drop its writer; an executor still running, or writing, after its terminal status no longer holds the stream open. The conformance harness reads the raw channel so nothing_after_terminal still sees such writes. The test failed before the change (stream open after 5 s). A cancelled task reaches its terminal state on the queue whatever its executor's cancel hook writes (2026-10-13): only the default hook wrote Canceled there, so CancelTask against a hook overridden to release state stored Canceled while the send stream ended after Working with no terminal frame, and a halt or shutdown left such a task Working. After a hook that returns Ok without a terminal state the handler writes Canceled itself (TerminalTracking::cancel_with). Both tests failed before the change.

entries.requirement: The agent MAY return a `Task` for complex processing with status/artifact updates
or MAY return a `Message` for direct streaming responses without task overhead.
entries.notes: A Message as the executor's first event is streamed as the whole response.

entries.requirement: The implementation MUST provide immediate feedback on progress and intermediate results.
entries.notes: The stream is returned before the executor finishes (the cooperative-executor test returns the stream while the executor waits on a Notify); events are broadcast as written. Disposition (audit register R33, approved 2026-10-14): a send stream's first frame waits for the executor's first event, with no time bound. Line 208 requires a message-only stream to contain exactly one Message, so a Task sent before the executor shows which kind of stream it is would break that MUST for an agent that answers with a Message; the executor's first event is the earliest the kind is known, so the wait ends there.

entries.requirement: GetTask TaskNotFoundError: The task ID does not exist or is not accessible.
When `includeArtifacts` is false (the default), the artifacts field MUST be omitted entirely from each Task object in the response.
entries.notes: Handler sets task.artifacts = None unless includeArtifacts is true, and serde skips None, so the field is absent. Tested on a task that has an artifact, for includeArtifacts absent and false, at the handler and on the REST wire; shown to fail with the default flipped.

entries.requirement: The `nextPageToken` field MUST always be present in the response.
entries.notes: Field is a plain String with no skip_serializing_if; gRPC follows proto3 default semantics.

entries.requirement: When there are no more results ... the field MUST be set to an empty string ("").
The operation MUST return only tasks visible to the authenticated client
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: met by the SDK, not left to the application. With an authenticating interceptor that identifies callers, caller isolation is the default (since 0.15): each caller's tasks are in a partition of their own, and ListTasks returns only that partition (Bob lists none of Alice's tasks). Without identities, or with share_tasks_across_callers(), tasks are visible tenant-wide by the deployer's choice. The earlier notes describing a default with no scoping were stale.

entries.requirement: and MUST use cursor-based pagination for performance and consistency.
Tasks MUST be sorted by last update time in descending order.
Implementations MUST implement appropriate authorization scoping to ensure clients can only access authorized tasks.
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: caller isolation scopes every operation to the caller's partition by default once callers are identified (in-memory, SQLite and PostgreSQL stores); a finer authorization model is the agent's, through ServerInterceptor (permission_denied).

entries.requirement: Implementations MUST return tasks sorted by their status timestamp time in descending order (most recently updated tasks first).
entries.notes: Tasks without a parseable status timestamp fall back to write order.

entries.requirement: TaskNotCancelableError: The task is not in a cancelable state
CancelTask TaskNotFoundError
SubscribeToTask UnsupportedOperationError: Streaming is not supported by the agent
entries.notes: SubscribeToTask against a card whose streaming capability is false or absent answers UnsupportedOperationError (-32004) over JSON-RPC (test added 2026-10-10, shown to fail with the check disabled). No-op when no card is configured; see §8.1 line 1970.

entries.requirement: SubscribeToTask TaskNotFoundError
UnsupportedOperationError: The operation is attempted on a task that is in a terminal state
The stream MUST terminate when the task reaches a terminal state
entries.notes: Every stream ends at the terminal event (in_memory.rs:1088-1097), and SubscribeToTask stays open across turns until one (STREAM-SUB-002, 2026-10-12). Since 2026-10-15 (maintainer decision) HandlerLimits::subscribe_max_idle is Option<Duration>, None by default, so a stream to a parked task no longer ends early at 300 s: it ends at the terminal state, when the task is deleted, or when the client goes, which every binding detects without the bound (SSE keep-alive write, WebSocket read loop and idle_timeout, gRPC tx.closed(), SLIMRPC session close; read 2026-10-15). An operator may still set a bound (with_subscribe_max_idle), which ends such a stream without a terminal state; that is a documented opt-out from this MUST, not the default. A store failure while waiting no longer ends the stream at the bound: it keeps polling and warns once per run of failures. A cancel whose executor hook writes nothing reaches the queue as Canceled (2026-10-13, see the 210 entry).

entries.requirement: The operation MUST return a `Task` object as the first event in the stream, representing the current state of the task at the time of subscription.
entries.notes: The Task is read at a known position (2026-10-13): the stream attaches to the queue first, at an exact position, and the task row is read once every event up to there is stored and none is being stored (streaming/event_queue/applied.rs), so the Task and the live events neither overlap nor leave a gap. Read before the attach, as until then, it trailed the broadcast and an event broadcast before the attach and stored after the read was in neither. The wait is bounded by subscribe_replay_catchup (2 s); past it the event log fills the gap after the Task. Outside the mark: a row CancelTask or another replica writes.

TaskNotFoundError (create)
The operation MUST establish a webhook endpoint for task update notifications.
entries.notes: A create with "id": "" is given an id (2026-10-13); it was stored under "", which Get and Delete refuse, and the next such create replaced it.

entries.requirement: The configuration MUST persist until task completion or explicit deletion.
entries.notes: No eviction/TTL in any push-config store; retention only purges terminal tasks. InMemoryPushConfigStore loses configs on process restart (inherent to in-memory).

entries.requirement: PushNotificationNotSupportedError (get)
entries.notes: Get answers PushNotificationNotSupported when the card does not declare pushNotifications or no push sender is wired (ensure_push_supported). Until 2026-10-13 Get checked the card only: with no sender it still ran against the store, answering what Create could never have stored.

entries.requirement: TaskNotFoundError: The push notification configuration does not exist.
The operation MUST return configuration details including webhook URL and notification settings.
entries.notes: Test asserts URL only; whole stored config is returned.

entries.requirement: The operation MUST fail if the configuration does not exist or the client lacks access.
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: a config that does not exist is PushConfigNotFound/TaskNotFound, and another caller's config is not found and cannot be deleted under caller isolation (the default with identified callers); the test added 2026-10-18 pins Get and Delete across callers, which no test covered.

entries.requirement: PushNotificationNotSupportedError (list)
entries.notes: List answers PushNotificationNotSupported when the card does not declare pushNotifications or no push sender is wired (ensure_push_supported). Until 2026-10-13 List checked the card only: with no sender it still ran against the store, answering what Create could never have stored.

entries.requirement: TaskNotFoundError: The task ID does not exist or is not accessible. (ListTaskPushNotificationConfigs)
entries.notes: RequestHandler::require_task checks the task before listing; an unknown task is TaskNotFound (REST 404, JSON-RPC -32001), as in the reference SDK. A test that asserted the old empty list was corrected.

entries.requirement: The operation MUST return all active push notification configurations for the specified task
and MAY support pagination for tasks with many configurations.
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-14 RequestHandler::on_list_push_configs_page pages the list on every binding (JSON-RPC and WebSocket params, HTTP+JSON and axum query, gRPC and SLIMRPC fields): ordered by id, at most pageSize, nextPageToken while more remain (base64url of the last id returned), InvalidField(pageToken) for one this server did not give, pageSize 0 read as unset. Without pageSize or pageToken the whole list is returned unordered, as before. Before: pageSize/pageToken were ignored and nextPageToken was always None; the list is bounded by max_push_configs_per_task either way.

entries.requirement: PushNotificationNotSupportedError (delete)
entries.notes: Delete answers PushNotificationNotSupported when the card does not declare pushNotifications or no push sender is wired (ensure_push_supported). Until 2026-10-13 Delete checked the card only: with no sender it still ran against the store, answering what Create could never have stored.

entries.requirement: TaskNotFoundError: The task ID does not exist. (DeleteTaskPushNotificationConfig)
entries.notes: The task must exist (TaskNotFound otherwise); deleting a config that is already gone on an existing task still succeeds, keeping the operation idempotent.

entries.requirement: The operation MUST permanently remove the specified push notification configuration.
entries.notes: Delivery re-lists configs per event (push_delivery/mod.rs:72), so later events are not sent to a deleted webhook; no test asserts 'no notification after delete'.

entries.requirement: This operation MUST be idempotent - multiple deletions of the same config have the same effect.
UnsupportedOperationError: The agent does not support authenticated extended cards
ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError: The agent declares support but does not have an extended agent card configured.
entries.notes: Returned when the handler's card declares the capability and no extended card is set with with_extended_agent_card (since 2026-10-14, audit register R68). Until then the public card was served in the extended card's place, and -32007 was returned only by a handler with no card at all, which now answers UnsupportedOperationError (see 3164).

entries.requirement: The client MUST authenticate the request using one of the schemes declared in the public AgentCard.securitySchemes and AgentCard.security fields.
entries.notes: Client: get_extended_agent_card does not check that credentials matching the card's schemes are attached; the caller must register an interceptor for one of them. For an APIKeySecurityScheme, AuthInterceptor::api_key sends the key in the header or cookie the scheme names, over JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON and gRPC (e2e against ApiKeyAuthInterceptor); until 2026-10-14 the only API-key path wrote Authorization, which such an agent refuses. A key placed in the query string goes in the request URL over JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON (since 2026-10-14, audit register R67; refused before, as no transport could add a query parameter), and the gRPC and WebSocket transports refuse the call with ClientError::InvalidAuthScheme rather than send it without the key. Server side refuses the call unless an authenticating interceptor exists (or allow_unauthenticated_extended_card opt-out).

entries.requirement: The operation MAY return different details based on client authentication level, including additional skills, capabilities, or configuration not available in the public Agent Card.
entries.notes: RequestHandlerBuilder::with_extended_agent_card sets the card served to an authenticated caller, distinct from the public one. Without it a card that declares the capability answers ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError (since 2026-10-14; the public card used to be served). One extended card for every authenticated caller: no per-caller variation (see 3144). Until 2026-10-14 the builder had no extended-card setting, so the 'extended' card was always the public one (audit register R56).

entries.requirement: Clients retrieving this extended card SHOULD replace their cached public Agent Card with the content received from this endpoint for the duration of their authenticated session or until the card's version changes.
entries.notes: The SDK caches a card in two places. A2aClient caches the capabilities it checks calls against (DeclaredCapabilities, from the card it was built from); since 2026-10-13 get_extended_agent_card replaces them with the extended card's (A2aClient::adopt_capabilities), keeping extendedAgentCard declared, and only when the client checks at all. Before, it kept the public card's, so a capability only the extended card declared was refused locally with CapabilityNotDeclared. The other, the resolver's, is replaced when the application calls CachingCardResolver::install_extended_card, which serves the extended card from resolve() until clear_extended_card() or invalidate(); the application decides when the session ends.

entries.requirement: Blocking (`return_immediately: false` or unset): The operation MUST wait until the task reaches a terminal state ... or an interrupted state ... before returning.
entries.notes: collect_events loops until `is_terminal() || is_interrupted()` (sync_collector.rs:242). Edge: if the executor returns without ever reaching a terminal/interrupted state, the collector drains (bounded by executor_drain_timeout) and answers with the non-terminal state (sync_collector.rs:205-221) -- an agent bug, but the SDK does not force a terminal state there.

entries.requirement: The response MUST include the latest task state with all artifacts and status information.
entries.notes: Artifacts are folded into the collected task and returned. Note the response omits `history` unless historyLength is set (respond.rs:36-48, decisions.rs:34), which the spec's 'implementation-defined default' for unset historyLength permits.

entries.requirement: Non-Blocking (`return_immediately: true`): The operation MUST return immediately after creating the task, even if processing is still in progress.
entries.notes: Returns the Submitted snapshot and spawns the background processor; test asserts state==Submitted and that the store later reaches Completed.

entries.requirement: historyLength 0: No history should be returned; the `history` field SHOULD be omitted
entries.notes: truncate_history returns None for n==0, so the field is omitted (not []) on GetTask, ListTasks and SendMessage responses.

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings MUST specify how service parameters are transmitted in their binding specification.
entries.notes: WebSocket: the binding specification (book/src/bindings/websocket.md §2) states the mechanism (upgrade headers, once per connection), the A2A-Version query fallback, value constraints, the reserved :path key, and that parameters cannot vary per request. SLIMRPC: slimrpc.md §3. The page's wire claims are pinned by websocket_binding_spec.rs (handshake refusal and query fallback, refusal codes and ErrorInfo, stream frames and marker), which passed against the page as written.

entries.requirement: A2A-Extensions: Comma-separated list of extension URIs that the client wants to use for the request (implied: server reads it as a service parameter; client can send it)
entries.notes: Server parses the lowercased `a2a-extensions` header/metadata on all bindings via build_call_context. Client, since 2026-10-13: ClientBuilder::with_extensions sends the URIs as one comma-separated header (gRPC metadata on gRPC) on every request an interceptor did not give the header, and WebSocketTransportConfig::with_extensions puts it on the upgrade, where the WebSocket server reads service parameters. extensions_e2e.rs checks what the executor sees on JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON, gRPC and WebSocket, unary and streaming. Not tested over SLIMRPC. Until then a caller had to set the header itself.

entries.requirement: A2A-Version: ... If the version is not supported, the agent returns VersionNotSupportedError
entries.notes: Every binding, the axum adapter included (validate_a2a_request middleware), answers VersionNotSupportedError.

entries.requirement: As service parameter names MAY need to co-exist with other parameters ... all service parameters defined by this specification will be prefixed with `a2a-`.
entries.notes: Naming rule for the spec itself; SDK constants use the `A2A-` prefix.

entries.requirement: Send Message operations MAY be idempotent. Agents may utilize the messageId to detect duplicate messages.
entries.notes: Implemented through an opt-in idempotency extension key in message metadata (IDEMPOTENCY_EXTENSION_URI), not by messageId alone.

entries.requirement: A duplicate cancellation request MAY return `TaskNotFoundError` if the task has already been canceled and purged.
entries.notes: Purged task -> TaskNotFound (store miss). A duplicate cancel of a still-stored Canceled task returns TaskNotCancelableError (cancel_task.rs:48), consistent with that error's definition though not literally 'the same effect' as the first cancel.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST return appropriate errors
entries.notes: Every ServerError maps to an ErrorCode, HTTP status and gRPC code; covered by per-code unit tests.

entries.requirement: Servers ... SHOULD provide actionable information to help clients resolve issues.
entries.notes: Refusals name the parameter and the accepted form or limit; the wire test pins six (message.id empty and too long, no parts, metadata over the size limit and not an object, unsupported A2A-Version). Shown to fail with the message.id label changed.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST reject requests with invalid or missing authentication credentials
entries.notes: The bundled ApiKey/Bearer/JWT interceptors refuse a missing or invalid credential with 401/UNAUTHENTICATED on every binding. Since 2026-10-18 build() refuses a card whose securityRequirements (top-level or a skill's, with no empty {} requirement making it optional) ask for a credential when no interceptor authenticates, unless authenticated_upstream() says a gateway in front checks it; so a handler can no longer serve a secured card unauthenticated by omission. tests/auth_every_method.rs calls every method in Method::ALL on JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON with no credential and a wrong one and requires 401 each time, with the valid token as the control (the official TCK has no test for this, findings §16 AUTH-SERVER-002).

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD include authentication challenge information in the error response
entries.notes: WWW-Authenticate added on HTTP bindings for 401. Since 2026-10-13 gRPC sends the same challenge as `www-authenticate` metadata on UNAUTHENTICATED, and SLIMRPC, whose errors carry no metadata, ends the message with `(WWW-Authenticate: <challenge>)`; both had dropped it. WebSocket answers per-message after upgrade with body only (auth/mod.rs doc), so no challenge there.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD specify which authentication scheme is required
entries.notes: Challenge carries the scheme (e.g. `Bearer realm="a2a"`), on HTTP as a header, on gRPC as metadata and on SLIMRPC in the message (since 2026-10-13 for the last two).

entries.requirement: Servers MUST return an authorization error when the authenticated client lacks required permissions
entries.notes: Hook: an interceptor returns A2aError::permission_denied -> 403 / PERMISSION_DENIED. Permission policy itself is the application's.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD indicate what permission or scope is missing (without leaking sensitive information ...)
entries.notes: permission_denied takes a caller-chosen message; SDK has no structured scope field.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST NOT reveal the existence of resources the client is not authorized to access
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: another caller's task answers exactly as an unknown id does (TaskNotFound, the test's control), from Get, Cancel, Subscribe and a continuing SendMessage, and their configs likewise; ACTS SEC-AUTH-003 and CORE-ERR-009 pass on three bindings. Since 2026-10-18 an unauthenticated push-config call is also refused for its credential before the capability check, so it learns nothing about the agent either.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST validate all input parameters before processing
entries.notes: validate_send_params runs before any side effect (ids, parts, input modes, metadata shape/size). Since 2026-10-13 also a message's referenceTaskIds (validate_id, as its taskId) and ListTasks' pageSize, which must be 1 to 100 (a2a.proto); both were accepted unchecked, the page size clamped to 1000 and 0 read as 50.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD specify which parameter(s) failed validation and why
entries.notes: Each handler validation message names the parameter (message.id, message, request metadata, A2A version); body-shape errors also carry a google.rpc.BadRequest field violation (jsonrpc_error_details.rs). The handler's own validation errors name the field in text only, not as a BadRequest detail: ServerError::InvalidParams carries a String, and changing it would break callers that match it.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD provide guidance on valid parameter values or formats
entries.notes: Messages state the limit or accepted value ("got 5000, max ...", "max 1048576", "must be a JSON object", "this server supports 1.0"); pinned by the wire test.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST return a not found error when a requested resource does not exist or is not accessible to the authenticated client
entries.notes: TaskNotFound (404/NOT_FOUND/-32001) for missing tasks and push configs on every binding.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD NOT distinguish between "does not exist" and "not authorized"
entries.notes: Tenant-scoped store returns None for another tenant's task, which surfaces as the same TaskNotFound.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD return appropriate error codes for temporary failures vs. permanent errors
entries.notes: Overloaded -> 503 with an AIP-193 status of RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED); Halted -> 503 / UNAVAILABLE; a rate-limit refusal -> 429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; internal -> 500 / INTERNAL. Until 2026-10-10 an overload's REST body read status INTERNAL under 503, naming a permanent failure. Since 2026-10-14 (audit register R57) a SQL store whose database cannot answer for now (pool timed out or closed, I/O, SQLite BUSY or LOCKED, Postgres connection, serialization, deadlock, lock, resource and shutdown codes) answers A2aError::unavailable: 503 / UNAVAILABLE, gRPC and SLIMRPC UNAVAILABLE; every database error was 500 / INTERNAL. A send and a push config's creation keep 500 / INTERNAL, since this SDK's client re-sends those on 503 as refused before processing.

entries.requirement: Servers MAY include retry guidance (e.g., Retry-After header in HTTP)
entries.notes: A rate-limit refusal carries Retry-After (whole seconds to the end of the window) on HTTP+JSON and a RetryInfo detail on the JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON, WebSocket and gRPC bindings. The SLIMRPC binding (bindings/a2a-protocol-slimrpc, error.rs) answers RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED without the delay: SLIMRPC errors have no details field. Overload (503) and halt (503) send no retry guidance: neither has a known end.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD log system errors for diagnostic purposes
entries.notes: Failures are recorded on the RPC span (error.type, otel.status_code=ERROR) and in metrics.on_error, and trace_error! logs a system error as an ERROR event at 19 call sites: executor failures and panics, failed task-store and queue writes, JSON-RPC and REST response serialization, failed audit writes, and a too-short HS256 secret. Since 2026-10-12 a test asserts the executor-failure event: an executor returning an internal error is logged at ERROR with the task id and the cause (three hand mutants killed: the call deleted, demoted to WARN, the cause dropped). The other sites use the same macro and are not tested one by one. Behind the `tracing` feature, on by default. Before: no test asserted that an internal error is logged.

entries.requirement: All error responses ... MUST convey ... Error Code ... Error Message
entries.notes: JSON-RPC {code,message,data}, REST AIP-193 {code,status,message,details}, gRPC Status(code,message,details).

entries.requirement: Each object in the [details] array MUST include a `@type` key
entries.notes: Every detail carries @type. An A2A error's ErrorInfo (and RetryInfo for a rate limit) comes from error_info_data. A2aError.data follows it as a typed detail (sse::error_details, used by JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON and WebSocket): as it is when it names its own string @type (a google.rpc.BadRequest), otherwise as a google.protobuf.Struct in the ProtoJSON Any form, {"@type": ..., "value": {...}}, with a non-object under value (since 2026-10-14, audit register R19; the fields were written beside @type, the form a2a-go writes, which a ProtoJSON Any decoder rejects). The gRPC binding sends the same data as BadRequest field violations or a Struct Any (dispatch/grpc/details.rs).

entries.requirement: Well-known types from the google.rpc error model (e.g., ErrorInfo, BadRequest) SHOULD be used where applicable
entries.notes: ErrorInfo on every A2A-specific error. Since ef31df9 a body or params that do not deserialize carry google.rpc.BadRequest with the field path (jsonrpc_error_details.rs, bad_request_details.rs). Since 2026-10-14 (audit register, the §3.3.2 row) the handler's own request checks carry a BadRequest naming the field too, through the new ServerError::InvalidField: ids (empty, too long, reference_task_ids), message.role, message.parts, every metadata and number-range check, a part's raw, the push config's required ids, taskId, url, authentication.scheme, token and credentials, ListTasks pageSize and statusTimestampAfter, and the REST query parameters. They named the field in the message only. Errors that name no single field (a per-task config limit, a card refused at build()) stay InvalidParams.

entries.requirement: Protocol bindings MUST map these elements to their native error representations while preserving semantic meaning
entries.notes: Per-code mappings to HTTP status and gRPC code are unit tested.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY accept additional messages for tasks in non-terminal states to enable multi-turn interactions
entries.notes: Non-terminal continuations reuse the task id; a send to a task whose executor is still running is refused (UnsupportedOperation), see tests.rs concurrent_send_to_in_flight_task_is_rejected. A continuation sent as soon as the task parks is built from the task as the previous turn left it (2026-10-13): it waits for that turn to store its events and reads the task again, where it used to save over what the turn had just stored, such as an artifact.

entries.requirement: When clients attempt to use operations or features that require capabilities not declared ... the agent MUST return an appropriate error response
entries.notes: Summary of 573-576 below, each TESTED. The checks are skipped only for a handler built with RequestHandlerBuilder::without_agent_card(), an explicit statement that it is not a public A2A server or that its card is published elsewhere; since 2026-10-12 build() refuses a handler with no card otherwise (spec §8.1). Before: every check was skipped whenever no card was configured, which was the default.

entries.requirement: If AgentCard.capabilities.pushNotifications is false or not present, push notification config operations (Create, Get, List, Delete) MUST return PushNotificationNotSupportedError
entries.notes: All four ops refuse when the card does not declare pushNotifications, and when no push sender is wired. build() refuses a card that declares pushNotifications with no sender, so a served card never advertises operations that refuse. Until 2026-10-13 only Create checked the sender and such a card was served.

entries.requirement: If AgentCard.capabilities.streaming is false or not present, SendStreamingMessage or SubscribeToTask MUST return UnsupportedOperationError
entries.notes: ensure_streaming_supported refuses SendStreamingMessage and SubscribeToTask unless capabilities.streaming is true. Tested over JSON-RPC for streaming false and absent (code -32004 on both methods, against an existing task); shown to fail with the check disabled. A no-op only for a handler built without_agent_card(); build() otherwise requires a card (2026-10-12).

entries.requirement: If AgentCard.capabilities.extendedAgentCard is false or not present, Get Extended Agent Card MUST return UnsupportedOperationError. If the agent declares support but has not configured an extended card, it MUST return ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError.
entries.notes: The handler's card decides: not declared, UnsupportedOperation; declared, the extended card if one is set, else ExtendedAgentCardNotConfigured (since 2026-10-14; the public card was served); no card at all, the extended card if one is set, else UnsupportedOperation (since 2026-10-14; it was NotConfigured).

entries.requirement: When a server requests use of an extension marked as `required: true` ... but the client does not declare support for it, the agent MUST return ExtensionSupportRequiredError
entries.notes: Every operation now refuses a client that does not declare a required extension; GetExtendedAgentCard was the one that skipped it.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD validate capability support by examining the Agent Card before attempting operations that require optional capabilities
entries.notes: A client built from a card refuses, before sending, every call that needs an optional capability the card does not set to true: streaming and resubscription (streaming), the four push-config methods and a send carrying an inline push config (pushNotifications), GetExtendedAgentCard (extendedAgentCard). The refusal is ClientError::CapabilityNotDeclared; nothing reaches the transport (tested against a recording transport for all ten call shapes). ClientBuilder::without_capability_checks and the CLI's --no-capability-check opt out; a client built from a bare URL has no card and checks nothing. Required extensions are not checked client-side: the client cannot know which it supports.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY generate a new contextId when processing a Message that does not include a contextId field
entries.notes: UUIDv4 generated.

entries.requirement: If an agent generates a new contextId, it MUST be included in the response (either Task or Message)
entries.notes: Task responses always carry context_id. A direct Message reply whose contextId the executor left empty now gets the task's contextId, on the blocking path and on a message-only stream; a contextId the executor set is kept. Until 2026-10-10 such a reply named no context.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY accept and preserve client-provided contextId values
entries.notes: Client contextId used verbatim after validation.

entries.requirement: If an agent cannot accept a client-provided contextId, it MUST reject the request with an error and MUST NOT generate a new contextId for the response
entries.notes: Invalid contextId -> InvalidParams before any task is created; a provided contextId is never replaced.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD NOT provide a client-generated contextId to a server unless they understand how the server will process that contextId
entries.notes: The client SDK never fills context_id itself; the caller builds the Message. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: whether to send a contextId of its own is a decision about the client's conversation, which only the caller can make; the SDK never generates one.

entries.requirement: Server-generated contextId values SHOULD be treated as opaque identifiers by clients
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the client keeps a server's contextId as the opaque ContextId newtype and never parses or derives anything from it.

entries.requirement: All tasks and messages with the same contextId SHOULD be treated as part of the same conversational session
entries.notes: SDK groups by context (find_task_by_context, per-context lock) and passes context_id to the executor; conversational semantics are the agent's. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: the SDK keys storage, locks and continuation on contextId and gives the executor the context's latest task (RequestContext::stored_task); what a conversational session means is the agent's.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY use the contextId to maintain internal state, conversational history, or LLM context
entries.notes: context_id exposed on RequestContext.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY implement context expiration or cleanup policies
entries.notes: Task-store TTL/capacity and retention modules.

entries.requirement: [Agents] SHOULD document any such policies
entries.notes: Deployment-specific; SDK documents its own TTL/capacity knobs in rustdoc. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: the SDK documents its own defaults (TaskStoreConfig: task_ttl, max_capacity; book deployment pages), but which policy a deployment runs, and where it tells its users, is the deployer's.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST generate a unique taskId for each new task they create
entries.notes: UUIDv4 per new task; test asserts a new id on a new round in the same context.

entries.requirement: The generated taskId MUST be included in the Task object returned to the client
entries.notes: Task.id is a required field; tests read task.id from the response and fetch it from the store.

entries.requirement: When a client includes a taskId in a Message, it MUST reference an existing task
entries.notes: Client-side obligation; the server enforces it (line 614). Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: which task a client means is the caller's knowledge; the server side of the same rule (TaskNotFound for an unknown taskId, §3.4.2 line 614) is TESTED.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST return a TaskNotFoundError if the provided taskId does not correspond to an existing task
Clients MAY include the contextId in subsequent messages
entries.notes: Message.context_id field exposed.

entries.requirement: Clients MAY use taskId (with or without contextId) to continue or refine a specific task
entries.notes: A refused continuation leaves the task it names as it was: an inline push config is registered before the turn touches the row, and a refusal no longer runs the new-task rollback that deleted the row (2026-10-13). When the config is accepted but the turn cannot be saved, a config the server created is withdrawn; one the request named by id stays, since it may have replaced the client's own.

entries.requirement: Clients MAY use contextId without taskId to start a new task within an existing conversation context
Agents MUST infer contextId from the task if only taskId is provided
Agents MUST reject messages containing mismatching contextId and taskId
entries.notes: Rejected with InvalidParams.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD use the referenceTaskIds field in Message to explicitly reference related tasks
entries.notes: Field exposed on Message; client SDK never sets it. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: which tasks are related is the caller's knowledge; Message::with_reference_task_ids (message.rs:223) sets the field, and the server resolves it since 2026-10-18 (RequestContext::referenced_tasks).

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD use referenced tasks to understand the context and intent of follow-up requests
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-18 the handler resolves message.referenceTaskIds into RequestContext::referenced_tasks before the executor runs: read in the caller's partition (another caller's task resolves to nothing, as GetTask does), unknown ids skipped, duplicates once, at most 16. Using them is the agent's: SUPPORTED.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD leverage the shared contextId to provide contextually relevant responses
entries.notes: The handler gives the executor the latest task stored for the message's contextId as RequestContext::stored_task, with its history, on every send that names a context; using it for relevance is the agent's.

entries.requirement: All implementations MUST deliver events in the order they were generated. Events MUST NOT be reordered during transmission
entries.notes: One broadcast channel per task, and writes to it take turns from the moment a position is assigned until the event is broadcast (2026-10-13), so writes in flight at once (CancelTask's beside the executor's, a terminal event held for the store's verdict) reach the persistence channel and every stream in position order. Until then a later write could overtake a held terminal event, and on a multi-threaded runtime any two writes could swap. The SSE, gRPC and WebSocket writers forward each stream sequentially.

entries.requirement: An agent MAY serve multiple concurrent streams to one or more clients for the same task
Events MUST be broadcast to all active streams for that task
Each stream MUST receive the same events in the same order
entries.notes: A stream that falls behind the bounded broadcast buffer now catches up from the task's event log, after the last position it delivered, and goes on live (2026-10-12), so a slow stream receives the same events in the same order as a fast one. Only a complete replay whose head is still in the log is used, and a live event that does not follow it is reported as a lag, so no stream skips an event silently. Since 2026-10-15 (maintainer decision) a replay longer than subscribe_replay_limit is read a page at a time, for a lag, a missed turn and a Last-Event-ID resume, and the stream reads the channel again only once the last page is in; before, a lag past the limit ended with streamLagged, and a resume past it skipped the positions between the replay's end and the live receiver's start with no streamLagged at all (event_log_tests pinned [snapshot, 1, 2] for a log of five). A page with a hole, an empty page, or a read cut short by the catch-up deadline never asks for more (log_replay_tests). After an independent review (2026-10-15): a resume whose first read the log had not caught up with skipped the rest silently, and now reads on while the log moves forward, reporting what it cannot supply; the hook answers a gap-free page the log covers even when it trails the writer, rather than nothing; a page the log cannot supply after a lag is reported once. Remaining, why PARTIAL/low, each ending the stream with an explicit streamLagged after what was delivered: a lag beyond what the log still holds (the in-memory stores keep 512 events per task by default; the SQL stores keep the whole log, so with them this case cannot arise short of a failed append), or a custom store without an event log. Every stream receives positions in the order they were assigned, because writes are broadcast in that order (2026-10-13, see spec line 683); before that a reader, which skips a position it has passed, could lose an event another write had overtaken. A SubscribeToTask stream across turns replays from the log what each reattach answer leaves it owing (2026-10-13): the events a turn broadcast before the reattach hook found its queue, a turn that ran between two polls and parked again or finished, and, on a replica sharing the store, the running replica's events, a poll late. Until then all of them were lost without a streamLagged. Without a log the turn's missed events are reported as streamLagged, and a turn numbered from 1 is no longer skipped as already delivered. A read dropped while the log is read keeps the replay owed, for a lag too. Since 2026-10-15 (audit register R69) a subscription with no local queue reads the task with the event-log position it reflects, in one store read (TaskStore::get_with_position), and replays the log after that position. It read the log's end and then the task: another replica's processor logs each event before it stores it, so an event logged before the first read and stored after the second was in neither the snapshot nor the replay and was lost with no streamLagged (reproduced by a test that fails on the old order), and one logged and stored between them arrived twice. Every shipped store records the position atomically with each write the processors make inside AppliedPosition::scope; a custom store that reports none falls back to the old order, which can still lose that one event. A turn after a failed append is numbered after the later of the log's end and the stored position, so its first event no longer takes the failed event's position and is not skipped as already delivered by a subscriber past it (found by an independent review of R69, 2026-10-15; the live-subscriber case predates R69). During a rolling upgrade a replica on an earlier release does not write the position, so a subscriber can receive events twice until every replica is upgraded. A continuation sent the moment a task parks no longer numbers its events over the previous turn's (2026-10-13): it was admitted when the executor returned, before the processor had logged the turn's last events, so its positions collided and its events were dropped from the log. A turn's queue is now released once its events are stored; within one process only. A replay with a position missing, which a failed append leaves, is not used either (2026-10-13): a lag across it is reported as streamLagged and a resume across it starts from the snapshot, where the stream used to skip the lost event silently.

entries.requirement: Closing one stream MUST NOT affect other active streams for the same task
entries.notes: Readers are independent broadcast::Receivers and nothing cancels a task when a stream closes. The test drops the originating SendStreamingMessage stream and checks a SubscribeToTask stream still reaches the terminal event. Not injection-proven: no single-point code fault produces the violation today; the test guards against adding one (e.g. cancel-on-disconnect).

entries.requirement: Patch version numbers SHOULD NOT be used in requests, responses and Agent Cards
entries.notes: A2A_VERSION = "1.0" used for headers and card builder; some test fixtures use "1.0.0" but no production path does.

entries.requirement: [Patch version numbers] MUST not be considered when clients and servers negotiate protocol versions
entries.notes: Neither side compares the patch. The server accepts a request whose A2A-Version names its Major.Minor, whatever follows (is_served_version). The client keeps the card's interfaces of protocol major 1 (is_compatible: "1.0.0" and "1.1-rc1" both count) in card order and sends 1.0, so it does not compare the minor either: a 1.1 interface listed first is chosen and addressed as 1.0.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST send the A2A-Version header with each request
entries.notes: All four transports set it; JSON-RPC/REST covered implicitly by e2e tests against the default (version-required) RestDispatcher/JsonRpcDispatcher. WebSocket sends it on the upgrade only (per connection). The agent card fetch sends it too since 2026-10-13 (it went without), unless the caller passes its own A2A-Version in CardFetchOptions. SLIMRPC sends it as the a2a-version metadata key. Its multicast client (SlimRpcMulticast) sent none until 2026-10-13, hidden by the SLIMRPC server accepting a missing version; the multicast tests now run against a server that requires it.

entries.requirement: Clients MAY provide the A2A-Version as a request parameter instead of a header.
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-15, opt-in: VersionQueryInterceptor adds A2A-Version=1.0 to every request's query parameters, which the JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON transports append to the URL; the header is still sent beside it, so a server reading both (this SDK's, dispatch/version.rs requested_version: header first, then the parameter) answers the same either way, and a proxy that drops unknown headers no longer drops the version. Sending the parameter instead of the header was not chosen: a server that reads only the header would take the request for 0.3. gRPC and WebSocket have no per-request query string and send the version as metadata.

entries.requirement: (implied) Server must honour A2A-Version supplied as a request parameter (`?A2A-Version=1.0`), since clients MAY send it that way and agents MUST process the requested version
entries.notes: dispatch::requested_version reads the header, else the ?A2A-Version= parameter, on JSON-RPC, REST, the WebSocket upgrade and axum.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST process requests using the semantics of the requested A2A-Version (matching Major.Minor).
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-12 (maintainer decision) a request is served only when its A2A-Version names this server's Major.Minor, 1.0, with any patch; any other version, 1.1 included, is VersionNotSupportedError naming 1.0, on every binding through one validator (the WebSocket handshake had its own copy). Until then any 1.x was accepted and served with 1.0 semantics, as the official Python SDK still does (_is_version_compatible compares the major only).

entries.requirement: If the version is not supported by the interface, agents MUST return a VersionNotSupportedError.
entries.notes: The axum adapter now validates A2A-Version like the other bindings.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST interpret empty value as 0.3 version.
entries.notes: Empty means 0.3 and is refused by default on every binding: JSON-RPC, REST, axum, WebSocket, gRPC and, since 2026-10-13, SLIMRPC, which until then served it as 1.0. Only the explicit opt-outs (accept_missing_version_header, gRPC with_require_version_header(false), SLIMRPC with_require_version(false)) serve it as 1.0; a server so configured is not conforming here, by the deployer's choice. PARTIAL until 2026-10-13: this note said every binding refused while SLIMRPC did not.

entries.requirement: Tooling libraries and SDKs ... MUST provide mechanisms to help clients manage protocol versioning, such as negotiation of the transport and protocol version used.
entries.notes: ClientBuilder::from_card filters interfaces by protocol major then binding preference; server exposes validate_version_metadata for out-of-tree bindings.

entries.requirement: Messages SHOULD NOT be used to deliver task outputs.
entries.notes: Agent's choice; SDK provides TaskUpdater-style artifact() helper. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: §3.1.1 allows a direct Message reply, so the SDK cannot tell output from communication; EventEmitter::artifact is the path it offers.

entries.requirement: Results SHOULD BE returned using Artifacts associated with a Task.
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: as the SHOULD NOT on the same line; artifacts are what EventEmitter::artifact writes.

entries.requirement: Clients using streaming ... MAY not receive all status update messages if the client is disconnected and then reconnects.
entries.notes: Informative allowance; SDK additionally offers SSE resumption (sse_resumption_e2e.rs) which narrows the gap.

entries.requirement: Messages MUST NOT be considered a reliable delivery mechanism for critical information.
entries.notes: Design guidance for agent/client authors; not testable in the SDK. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: a design rule for agent and client authors; the SDK's own critical signals (failure class, approval, provenance) ride in Task.status and task metadata, which GetTask returns, not in messages.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY choose to persist all Messages that contain important information in the Task history
entries.notes: SDK persists every agent Message event into Task.history (capped at 1024).

entries.requirement: clients MUST NOT rely on this behavior unless negotiated out-of-band.
entries.notes: Client-author obligation. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: an obligation on client authors; the SDK client reads task state from Task and status events, not from message history.

entries.requirement: All protocol bindings MUST provide functionally equivalent representations of these data structures.
entries.notes: One domain model (serde JSON) with a prost conversion layer for gRPC; golden fixtures from the official Python SDK prove JSON<->proto equivalence. What a client sends is checked since 2026-10-13 (make_portable): a raw part must be base64, read as the gRPC conversion reads it and kept in standard padded form; an integer beyond ±2^53 in metadata or a data part, which the gRPC conversion refuses, is InvalidParams. Before, any such value was stored, and the task could not be read over gRPC (GetTask, ListTasks pages with it and SubscribeToTask answered INTERNAL). An executor's events are held to the same rules at the queue writer since 2026-10-14 (content.rs make_portable, audit register R64), in every event kind and in a task snapshot's status, artifacts and history: a raw part that is not base64, an integer beyond ±2^53, or a metadata that is not a JSON object (all a google.protobuf.Struct holds) is InvalidParams before the event is persisted or broadcast, and raw is kept in standard padded form. Before, such an artifact was served over JSON and failed a gRPC read. A task store written before the check can still hold one; the gRPC stream then ends at it (dispatch/grpc/native.rs reader_to_native_stream_stops_after_a_conversion_error).

entries.requirement: The agent MUST include authentication credentials in the request headers as specified in the PushNotificationConfig.authentication field.
entries.notes: The sender writes Authorization for Bearer and Basic (case-insensitive), as a2a-go v2.5.0 does. A config naming any other scheme is now refused at creation with InvalidParams, so no webhook is called without the credentials its config specifies. Until 2026-10-10 such a config was stored and delivered without credentials (a2a-go still does that). The sender's runtime drop remains for configs stored before. Since 2026-10-13 a token or credentials a header cannot carry (CR, LF or another control character) is InvalidParams at creation, inline or by CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig; it was stored and refused at every delivery. v1.0.1's text names PushNotificationConfig, which the v1.0.1 proto does not define: the message with `authentication` is TaskPushNotificationConfig (a2a.proto line 469), the name upstream main uses since.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST respond with HTTP 2xx status codes to acknowledge successful receipt
entries.notes: Binds the webhook receiver (client-side app). SDK ships no webhook receiver; only `push::webhook::notification_token` header helper. Sender side treats any 2xx as success (sender.rs:925).

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD process notifications idempotently, as duplicate deliveries may occur
entries.notes: Webhook receiver concern; no SDK receiver/dedup hook provided.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST validate the task ID matches an expected task
entries.notes: Webhook receiver concern; SDK provides no receiver or task-id validation helper (only token header extraction).

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD implement appropriate security measures to verify the notification source
entries.notes: SDK hook: sender emits the config token under both X-A2A-Notification-Token and A2A-Notification-Token; receiver can read it with webhook::notification_token. Verification itself is the app's.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST attempt delivery at least once for each configured webhook
entries.notes: Every configured webhook is attempted for every event, on the background and blocking paths. push_delivery_budget now sets concurrency: ceil(configs / (budget / timeout)), at least 1, at most configs (17 at the defaults); events go in order per webhook. Until 2026-10-11 deliveries were sequential and the budget skipped the rest (6 of 100 reached at defaults). PushRetryPolicy max_attempts 0 is taken as 1 (setter and loop). Not covered: a webhook whose single attempt exceeds push_delivery_timeout is cut off, which is an attempt, not a skip.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY implement retry logic with exponential backoff for failed deliveries
entries.notes: PushRetryPolicy default 3 attempts, backoff [1s,2s]; only 5xx/408/429/transport errors are retried.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD include a reasonable timeout for webhook requests (recommended: 10-30 seconds)
entries.notes: HttpPushSender's per-request timeout defaults to 10s and HandlerLimits::push_delivery_timeout, which bounds a whole delivery with its retries, to 30s: both inside the recommended 10-30s. At the defaults every attempt of the three-attempt schedule starts inside the bound (5s, 16s, 28s when each request runs to its timeout); the first two finish. Until 2026-10-12 the bound was 5s and truncated the schedule to one attempt.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY stop attempting delivery after a configured number of consecutive failures
entries.notes: max_attempts per delivery; non-retryable 4xx stops immediately.

entries.requirement: Extensions SHOULD include version information in their URI identifier.
entries.notes: The four extensions the SDK authors carry /v1 in their URIs; since 2026-10-18 build() warns about a card extension URI with no version in it (no digit at all, a deliberately loose test).

entries.requirement: A new URI MUST be created for breaking changes to an extension.
entries.notes: Process requirement on extension authors; not code-testable.

entries.requirement: If a client requests a version of an extension that the agent does not support, the agent SHOULD ignore the extension for that interaction and proceed without it
entries.notes: Activated set is the exact-string intersection of A2A-Extensions request header and card-declared URIs; undeclared URIs are silently ignored and not echoed.

entries.requirement: unless the extension is marked as required in the AgentCard, in which case the agent MUST return an error indicating unsupported extension
entries.notes: Handler-level check (all bindings; gRPC metadata is converted to the same header map) returns ExtensionSupportRequiredError (-32008) naming missing URIs. Note: GetExtendedAgentCard does not call ensure_required_extensions (extended_card.rs has no call).

entries.requirement: It MUST NOT fall back to a previous version of the extension automatically.
entries.notes: Extension URIs match by exact string equality: a client declaring .../v2 neither satisfies a required .../v1 nor activates an optional one. Shown to fail with version-agnostic matching injected.

entries.requirement: Identical Functionality: Provide the same set of operations and capabilities
entries.notes: All 11 operations are routed on JSON-RPC, REST, gRPC and WebSocket (TCK --equivalence). WebSocket's leftover v0.3 alias message/stream was removed on 2026-10-12 and is now -32601 as over HTTP; shown to fail with the alias restored.

entries.requirement: Consistent Behavior: Return semantically equivalent results for the same requests
entries.notes: All bindings dispatch to the same RequestHandler; TCK compares task views across the four bindings in CI. Proto3 defaults on the JSON bindings are unset on ingress since 2026-10-13, as the gRPC conversion reads them: a part's mediaType and filename, a push config's id and token, ListTasks' contextId, pageToken and status. Before, JSON read them as values: an empty mediaType was refused as ContentTypeNotSupported, a config was stored under id "", and ListTasks listed nothing, where gRPC accepted, minted an id and listed everything. Each test failed before the change. Also since 2026-10-13, a raw part that is not base64 and an integer beyond ±2^53, neither of which gRPC can carry, are refused on the JSON bindings rather than stored.

entries.requirement: Same Error Handling: Map errors consistently using appropriate protocol-specific codes
entries.notes: Single ErrorCode table drives HTTP status, gRPC code and JSON-RPC code. A malformed query value on HTTP+JSON is InvalidParams as on JSON-RPC and gRPC (2026-10-13); it was read as absent. A gRPC error carries its data as the JSON bindings do (2026-10-13): a BadRequest as google.rpc.BadRequest, any other data as a google.protobuf.Struct detail, and a stream's error as a unary call's. gRPC dropped data, and a stream's error was INTERNAL "event queue error", so a lagged stream could not be told from an executor failure; the gRPC client decodes the details back into data.

entries.requirement: Equivalent Authentication: Support the same authentication schemes declared in the AgentCard
entries.notes: Auth is enforced by handler-level interceptors common to all bindings; CI runs a secured SUT and checks rejection+acceptance on all four bindings (tck.yml:217).

entries.requirement: Agents MUST declare all supported protocols in their AgentCard
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-18 every SDK listener (Server for JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON through Dispatcher::protocol_binding, WebSocket, gRPC) warns when it starts if the handler's static card declares no interface with its binding. A warning, not a refusal: many deployments and fixtures serve a card from one listener that names others, and a dynamic card is produced elsewhere. Declaring is the agent author's; the SDK reports the omission it can see.

entries.requirement: Clients MAY choose any protocol declared by the agent
entries.notes: from_card_preferring / with_protocol_binding.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD implement fallback logic for alternative protocols
entries.notes: Fallback is build-time only (next interface when the chosen one cannot be constructed); there is no runtime fallback on connection failure.

entries.requirement: All A2A-specific errors defined in Section 3.3.2 MUST be mapped to binding-specific error representations.
entries.notes: ErrorCode enum is the single source; http_status()/grpc_status() derive per-binding codes; gRPC adds google.rpc.ErrorInfo.

entries.requirement: (table) TaskNotFoundError -> JSON-RPC -32001, gRPC NOT_FOUND, HTTP 404

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings MUST define equivalent error code mappings that preserve the semantic meaning of each A2A error type.
entries.notes: WebSocket reuses the JSON-RPC codes verbatim, documented in its binding spec §5. Remaining: SLIMRPC's RpcCode mapping for PushNotSupported/UnsupportedOperation/VersionNotSupported (UNIMPLEMENTED) differs from A2A §5.4's gRPC column (FAILED_PRECONDITION); this is the SLIMRPC spec's own mapping (2977, maintainer/upstream). Reclassified PARTIAL to TESTED on 2026-10-14 (audit register, the §12/§5.4 row, approved): UNIMPLEMENTED preserves the meaning the A2A types carry (the operation is not available here), as SLIMRPC's own canonical mapping requires; the difference from the gRPC column is for the maintainer to report upstream (draft prepared, not filed).

entries.requirement: The binding specification SHOULD provide a similar mapping table showing how each A2A error type is represented in the custom binding's native error format.
entries.notes: WebSocket now has an error mapping table (binding spec §5). Remaining: SLIMRPC's vendored upstream table omits -32007/-32008/-32009.

entries.requirement: All JSON serializations of the A2A protocol data model MUST use camelCase naming for field names
entries.notes: All Serialize structs carry rename_all=camelCase (scripted scan found none with snake_case fields lacking it); snake_case accepted as input alias only (proto_field_alias.rs).

entries.requirement: Enum values MUST be represented according to the ProtoJSON specification ... (typically SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE).
entries.notes: TaskState/Role (the only proto enums) serialize as TASK_STATE_*/ROLE_*; legacy lowercase accepted as aliases on input.

entries.requirement: Protocol Buffer enum: TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED -> JSON value: "TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED"
entries.notes: Keyword appears only inside an enum identifier in an example; covered by the §5.5 enum entry.

entries.requirement: When serialized to JSON ... timestamps MUST be represented as ISO 8601 formatted strings in UTC timezone.
entries.notes: Every executor event passes the queue writer, which stamps an empty status timestamp with UTC now, rewrites one with a non-Z offset to the same instant in UTC (millisecond precision), and refuses one that does not parse as ISO 8601. Until 2026-10-10 an executor-set value went out unchanged on JSON-RPC/REST/WebSocket. Not covered: a Task an application writes straight to the task store, bypassing the queue. Since 2026-10-13 a timestamp is kept as written only in the canonical shape (T, Z, no offset): a lower-case t or z is rewritten as an offset is, and the parser reads RFC 3339 exactly as the gRPC conversion does, so a value served over JSON is one gRPC can carry.

entries.requirement: Millisecond precision SHOULD be used where available
entries.notes: utc_now_iso8601 formats YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ.

entries.requirement: Clients and servers MUST parse and generate ISO 8601 timestamps correctly
entries.notes: Server rejects malformed statusTimestampAfter with InvalidParams; JSON-path clients keep timestamps as opaque strings (no parsing needed). Until 2026-10-13 the parser was lenient (whitespace, unpadded or signed fields, an offset without minutes, 02-30 rolled into March) and refused every pre-1970 instant, so the JSON and gRPC bindings disagreed on such values and a 1969 statusTimestampAfter was InvalidParams. It now reads exactly what the time crate's RFC 3339 parser reads, checked over 1,655,808 strings, and the formatter writes pre-1970 instants as themselves.

entries.requirement: When millisecond precision is not available, the fractional seconds portion MAY be omitted or zero-filled
entries.notes: Parser accepts with and without fractional seconds.

entries.requirement: Timestamps MUST NOT include timezone offsets other than 'Z' (all times are UTC)
entries.notes: Every executor event passes the queue writer, which stamps an empty status timestamp with UTC now, rewrites one with a non-Z offset to the same instant in UTC (millisecond precision), and refuses one that does not parse as ISO 8601. Until 2026-10-10 an executor-set value went out unchanged on JSON-RPC/REST/WebSocket. Not covered: a Task an application writes straight to the task store, bypassing the queue. Since 2026-10-13 a timestamp is kept as written only in the canonical shape (T, Z, no offset): a lower-case t or z is rewritten as an offset is, and the parser reads RFC 3339 exactly as the gRPC conversion does, so a value served over JSON is one gRPC can carry.

entries.requirement: ...annotations to indicate whether fields are REQUIRED. These annotations serve as both documentation and validation hints
entries.notes: Descriptive; requirements are in the next entries.

entries.requirement: Fields marked REQUIRED indicate that the field MUST be present and set in valid messages.
entries.notes: Non-Option serde fields make absence a parse error (InvalidParams); ids validated non-empty/bounded by validate_id.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD validate these requirements and reject messages with missing required fields.
entries.notes: Inbound requests validated by typed deserialization plus explicit checks.

entries.requirement: Arrays marked as required MUST contain at least one element.
entries.notes: Enforced for Message.parts and Artifact.parts (before), and since 2026-10-11 for the published AgentCard: validate refuses empty defaultInputModes, defaultOutputModes, skills, or a skill's tags; build() runs it, the dynamic handler answers 500 for an invalid produced card, hot reload refuses one. Remaining, why PARTIAL/low: (1) ListTasksResponse.tasks is REQUIRED-repeated in the proto yet legitimately empty for a listing with no matches, a contradiction inside the specification; the SDK returns the empty list. (2) closed 2026-10-14: HotReloadAgentCardHandler::try_update validates as reload_from_json does and update is deprecated; served through DynamicAgentCardHandler, a card from new or update that does not validate is answered 500 rather than served (dynamic_handler.rs an_invalid_produced_card_is_not_served). The contradiction in (1) is reported upstream by the maintainer (draft, not filed). Client-side parsing stays tolerant on purpose. Since 2026-10-13 StaticAgentCardHandler::new runs the same checks (InvalidParams); a card handed to it directly was served unchecked. Since 2026-10-14 the queue writer also refuses an executor message (event, status message, snapshot history) with no parts and a snapshot artifact with no parts (R36).

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD ignore unrecognized fields in messages
entries.notes: No deny_unknown_fields anywhere in types/server/client src. The oneof wrappers skip unknown keys too: SendMessageResponse, StreamResponse and OAuthFlows through oneof_deserialize! (Part and SecurityScheme have their own deserializers), while still refusing no member or two. Until 2026-10-13 those three derived serde's externally tagged encoding, which failed on any key beside the member, so a response, a stream event or a card's flows carrying a field from a later version did not parse.

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings SHOULD be identified by a URI.
entries.notes: WebSocket: https://a2a-rust.com/bindings/websocket/v1; SlimRPC: https://a2a-protocol.org/bindings/experimental-slimrpc/v1.

entries.requirement: The protocolBinding field in the Agent Card's supportedInterfaces entry SHOULD be a URI
entries.notes: The SDK's own custom bindings are URIs (WEBSOCKET_BINDING_URI; SLIMRPC's upstream URI), and since 2026-10-18 build() warns about a custom protocolBinding that is not a URI. The card's content stays the author's.

entries.requirement: When a breaking change is introduced to a binding, a new URI MUST be used
entries.notes: Process requirement; both custom-binding URIs carry /v1, no breaking revision exists yet.

entries.requirement: UTF-8 encoding MUST be used for JSON text
entries.notes: serde_json emits UTF-8 and rejects invalid UTF-8. A body with a Latin-1 byte answers -32700 on JSON-RPC and 400 on HTTP+JSON; shown to fail with lossy decoding injected.

entries.requirement: Content MUST be validated against the A2A protocol schema before processing
entries.notes: Typed deserialization plus handler validation before executor invocation.

entries.requirement: Implementations MUST sanitize user-provided content to prevent injection attacks
entries.notes: SDK guards header injection in push creds (validate_header_value) and path traversal in REST; sanitising message content for downstream use is the executor's job. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: injection depends on where content ends up, which only the agent knows. The SDK sanitizes what it uses itself: ids (handler/helpers.rs), REST path traversal (dispatch/rest), push header values (push/sender.rs).

entries.requirement: File references within A2A messages MUST be validated to prevent SSRF
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the SDK never dereferences a Part's URL, so the fetch is the agent's; what it needs is now public. url_guard::check_public_url refuses private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, ULA and IPv4-mapped addresses, numeric IPv4 spellings and internal names (the push sender's checks, moved here); url_guard::resolve_public_url also resolves the host under a timeout and refuses it if any address is private, returning the address to connect to. RequestHandlerBuilder::refuse_private_file_urls() refuses such a message before the executor runs (form only, no DNS). SUPPORTED, not TESTED: the check is opt-in, because an SDK that never fetches has no reference to protect by default; an executor that fetches must call resolve_public_url.

entries.requirement: Authentication and authorization MUST be enforced as specified in Section 7
entries.notes: Section 7 enforcement as the SDK carries it: authentication interceptors on every method and binding, build() refusing a secured card nothing enforces (since 2026-10-18), the extended card gated on an authenticator, caller isolation by default with an authenticator (§13.1). Authorization policy beyond that is the agent's (§13.1 3099).

entries.requirement: Sensitive information in task history and artifacts MUST be protected according to applicable data protection regulations
entries.notes: Deployment/regulatory obligation. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: which regulation applies is the deployment's. The SDK's means: EncryptedTaskStore (feature encryption) for task content at rest, PushConfigCipher for push credentials, AuditLog::with_privacy, retention purges.

entries.requirement: The A2A-Version value MUST be in the format Major.Minor
entries.notes: Client sends "1.0" on all transports. The server accepts the value only when it names its own Major.Minor, 1.0, with any patch (is_served_version), and answers VersionNotSupportedError otherwise; until 0.15 it accepted any 1.x.

entries.requirement: The resource at this URI MUST return an AgentCard object
entries.notes: 404 when no card configured.

entries.requirement: The Agent Card MAY contain public information about an agent's capabilities
[Agent Card] SHOULD NOT include sensitive credentials or internal implementation details
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: a card carrying a credential in any URL (user information, or a query parameter named like a secret) is refused by build(), the static, dynamic and hot-reload handlers and per-caller extended cards; a URL naming an internal host (private address, .internal, .local, .lan, .corp, .intranet) is reported by card_warnings, which build() logs. Residual, the author's: a credential or internal detail in free text (a description, metadata) is not detected, since nothing distinguishes it from prose.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD support HTTPS to ensure authenticity and integrity of the Agent Card
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-14 serve::Server terminates TLS (Server::with_tls, with_tls_pem; tls-rustls, on by default in a2a-protocol-sdk), so the agent card and every JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON call can be served over HTTPS by the process itself; gRPC has had it since grpc-tls. The client fetches over HTTPS (rustls). Still plaintext: the quick-start serve/serve_with_addr and the WebSocket listener, which the deployment page puts behind a TLS-terminating proxy. Before: only gRPC terminated TLS.

entries.requirement: Agent Cards MAY be signed using JWS
entries.notes: Signing/verification in a2a-protocol-types::signing.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD verify signatures when present
entries.notes: With CardFetchOptions::with_signature_keys (feature signing), resolve_agent_card_with_options and fetch_card_from_url_with_options return a signed card only if one signature verifies against the caller's keys; a tampered card or one with no matching key fails the fetch, and so does an unsigned card unless with_require_signature(false), which verifies signatures only when present (until 2026-10-14 an unsigned card was returned, so removing a card's signatures let an altered card through; audit register R9).
