Since 2026-10-14 the other two ways a client gets a card take keys too: CachingCardResolver::with_options(CardFetchOptions), and ClientBuilder::from_signed_card(json, keys) for a card the caller holds, which verifies the JSON as given (audit register, §14 line 3344). Verification needs keys only the application can trust, so it is opt-in on every path; jku is never followed (the card cannot vouch for its own keys, §8.4.3 line 2122). Since 2026-10-14 the fetch verifies the card as received, before reading it into an AgentCard; it verified the typed card, so a correctly signed card from a peer that models a field this SDK does not was refused.

entries.requirement: Extended Agent Cards ... MAY contain additional information
entries.notes: with_extended_agent_card (since 2026-10-14) sets an extended card with whatever the operator adds; before, the handler served the public card.

entries.requirement: [Extended Agent Cards] MUST enforce appropriate access controls
entries.notes: Refuses unless an authenticating interceptor is registered or operator opts out explicitly.

entries.requirement: All legacy names and anchors MUST remain resolvable until the stated earliest removal version.
entries.notes: Spec-document anchor requirement.

entries.requirement: Each legacy span SHOULD be placed adjacent to the current object's heading
entries.notes: Spec-document editorial requirement.

entries.requirement: Client Implementations SHOULD: prefer new names; implement dual-handling; log a warning when receiving legacy-named objects
entries.notes: New names emitted. Dual-handling: legacy enum spellings and AgentCard.url parse (types crate aliases); since 2026-10-14 a fetched or extended card's v0.3 url, preferredTransport and additionalInterfaces fold into supportedInterfaces, and supportsAuthenticatedExtendedCard or App. A.2.2's supportsExtendedAgentCard is read as capabilities.extendedAgentCard (a field the v1.0 form sets wins), with a tracing warning naming each legacy field (legacy_card.rs). Not handled: App. A.2.1's kind discriminator on parts and stream events, which only a v0.3 interface sends; interface selection never picks one (ClientBuilder::from_card passes over a 0.3 interface for a 1.x one and refuses a card with none), so the client receives no such object. Before: no fallback for the extended-card field, url parsed but not folded, and no warning.

entries.requirement: Server Implementations MAY accept both legacy and current request message forms; emit only current form
entries.notes: Aliases accept legacy input; skip_serializing keeps output current-form.

entries.requirement: Until then, edits MUST be manual and reviewed in PRs affecting a2a.proto.
entries.notes: Spec-repo process.

entries.requirement: Production deployments **MUST** use encrypted communication (HTTPS for HTTP-based bindings, TLS for gRPC).
entries.notes: Binds production deployments. Since 2026-10-18 every listener the SDK starts can terminate TLS itself: Server::with_tls / with_tls_pem for JSON-RPC and REST (feature tls-rustls, since 2026-10-14), WebSocketDispatcher::with_tls / with_tls_pem for wss:// (2026-10-18), GrpcDispatcher::with_tls (grpc-tls); the client speaks HTTPS and wss:// by default (tls-rustls). The axum adapter leaves the listener, and so TLS, to the operator. Whether a deployment is production, and terminates TLS here or in front, stays the deployer's: SUPPORTED, not TESTED, because the requirement is on the deployment. Until 2026-10-18 these notes said the JSON-RPC/REST/WebSocket listeners were plaintext only; that was stale for HTTP after Server::with_tls (2026-10-14) and is no longer true for WebSocket.

entries.requirement: Implementations **SHOULD** use modern TLS configurations (TLS 1.3+ recommended) with strong cipher suites.
entries.notes: rustls 0.23.45 implements only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 (its versions.rs defines no other SupportedProtocolVersion), so SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0/1.1 cannot be offered. The client's config negotiates TLS 1.3 with a server that has it and enables only forward-secret AEAD suites (TLS13_* and TLS_ECDHE_*_GCM/CHACHA20_POLY1305); shown to fail with the client limited to TLS 1.2. TLS 1.2 stays enabled for peers without 1.3. The push sender's default config (push/sender.rs) uses the same builder chain; it is read, not handshake-tested.

entries.requirement: A2A Clients **SHOULD** verify the A2A Server's identity by validating its TLS certificate against trusted certificate authorities (CAs) during the TLS handshake.
entries.notes: Default config uses webpki Mozilla roots; extra roots via tls_config_with_extra_roots; no insecure-skip-verify path found.

entries.requirement: **MUST** authenticate every incoming request based on the provided credentials and its declared authentication requirements.
entries.notes: Interceptors run before every method on every binding (WebSocket per message). Since 2026-10-18 the card's declared requirements are tied to the chain: build() refuses a card requiring credentials with no authenticating interceptor (opt-out authenticated_upstream() for a gateway), and an authenticating interceptor that checks none of the declared schemes (ServerInterceptor::checks_scheme, answered by the bundled authenticators). Every method is shown refused without a credential on both HTTP bindings (auth_every_method.rs). The note that WebSocket per-message auth had no test was stale: websocket_binding_spec.rs and sdk auth_rejection_e2e.rs cover it.

entries.requirement: **SHOULD** use appropriate binding-specific error codes for authentication challenges or rejections.
entries.notes: HTTP 401/403, gRPC UNAUTHENTICATED/PERMISSION_DENIED; WebSocket answers in-body only (no status available after upgrade), untested.

entries.requirement: **SHOULD** provide relevant authentication challenge information with error responses.
entries.notes: WWW-Authenticate: `Bearer realm="a2a"` / `ApiKey header="x-api-key"` on HTTP 401s (JSON-RPC, REST, axum).

entries.requirement: Authorization logic is implementation-specific and **MAY** consider: skills, actions, data access policies, OAuth scopes
entries.notes: Custom ServerInterceptor returning A2aError::permission_denied; caller identity on CallContext.

entries.requirement: MUST use a Task to track the operation it is performing
entries.notes: Every SendMessage gets a stored Task before the executor runs (create.rs build_initial_task, respond.rs), so an executor asking for authorization always has one; the test shows the answer to such a send is a Task in AUTH_REQUIRED.

entries.requirement: MUST transition the TaskState to `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED`
entries.notes: EventEmitter::auth_required(explanation) (since 2026-10-18) makes the transition; executors writing events by hand can still emit the state directly.

entries.requirement: MUST include a TaskStatus message explaining the required authorization, unless the details of the authorization have been negotiated out-of-band or via an extension
entries.notes: EventEmitter::auth_required always writes the explanation as the status message, with the task's ids. An AUTH_REQUIRED written by hand with no message is logged as a warning at the queue (status_stamp.rs), not refused: the requirement exempts details negotiated out of band or by an extension, which only the executor knows.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST arrange to receive credentials via an out-of-band means, unless an in-band mechanism has been negotiated out-of-band or via an extension.
entries.notes: No SDK mechanism; agent-specific. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: the out-of-band channel is specific to the credential (a device flow, a consent page); EventEmitter::auth_required explains it to the client, and the stream stays open while the executor waits for it (TESTED, §7.6.1 line 1931).

entries.requirement: If the credential is received out-of-band, the agent SHOULD maintain any active response streams with the client after setting the TaskState to `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED`.
entries.notes: The server stream ends on a terminal state or when the executor's queue closes, not on an interrupted state. The test streams a task that parks at AUTH_REQUIRED, receives its credential out of band (the client sends nothing) and finishes: the same stream carries it to Completed.

entries.requirement: The agent MAY immediately continue Task processing after receiving the credential, without a requirement that clients send a follow-up message.
entries.notes: An executor may keep writing events after AUTH_REQUIRED; the test continues on the same run after an out-of-band credential with no follow-up message.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD support receiving messages directed to the Task while the Task remains in `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED`.
entries.notes: Test asserts an authenticated continuation to an AUTH_REQUIRED task is accepted and re-runs the executor (runs==2).

entries.requirement: The client SHOULD follow all In-Task Authorization Agent Responsibilities.
entries.notes: Binds a client that is itself an agent. EventEmitter::relay_auth_required(&downstream_status) (since 2026-10-18) moves its own task to AUTH_REQUIRED with the downstream explanation as a message of its own, meeting §7.6.1's three duties; whether to relay is the agent's call.

entries.requirement: a client SHOULD perform one of the following: Subscribe to Task / Register a webhook / Begin polling the Task
entries.notes: All three hooks exist; client EventStream only finishes on a terminal StatusUpdate (is_terminal, event_stream.rs:688), so it keeps reading after AUTH_REQUIRED. No automatic behaviour.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD receive credentials for in-task authorization requests out of band via a secure channel, such as HTTPS.
entries.notes: Not an SDK concern. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: the out-of-band channel is outside A2A and outside the SDK's listeners.

entries.requirement: Credentials SHOULD be bound to the agent which originated the request
entries.notes: No SDK support for credential binding in in-band exchange. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: applies only to in-band exchange, which v1.0.1 leaves to extensions; the SDK defines none.

entries.requirement: Credentials containing sensitive information SHOULD be only readable by the agent which originated the request, such as by encrypting the credential.
entries.notes: No SDK support. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: as 1961.

entries.requirement: A2A Servers **MUST** make an Agent Card available.
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-12 RequestHandlerBuilder::build() refuses a handler with no agent card unless told without_agent_card() (for a card published elsewhere, or a handler that is not a public A2A server). Every listener serves the card at GET/HEAD /.well-known/agent-card.json: JSON-RPC, REST and axum on their routes, and since 2026-10-14 the WebSocket listener (the request line is peeked and a card fetch answered as HTTP/1.1; anything else goes to the handshake) and the gRPC router (a `.well-known` service, with HTTP/1.1 accepted when there is a card). GrpcDispatcher::into_service, for a server the caller builds, is the A2A service alone. Before: the WebSocket and gRPC dispatchers served no card, so a deployment on either alone published none (PARTIAL); before 2026-10-12 agent_card defaulted to None and build() accepted that, serving 404.

entries.requirement: The AgentCard **MUST** properly declare supported protocols
entries.notes: build() refuses an interface with an empty url, binding or version (AgentCard::validate); since 2026-10-18 a served binding the card does not declare, and an interface URL that is not absolute, are warned about. Accuracy of the content stays the author's.

entries.requirement: The `supportedInterfaces` field **SHOULD** declare all supported protocol combinations in preference order
entries.notes: A listener serving a binding the card omits is warned about (since 2026-10-18), which covers 'all'; the order is the agent's stated preference and the client honours it (from_card).

entries.requirement: Each interface **MUST** accurately declare its transport protocol and URL
entries.notes: AgentInterface::jsonrpc/grpc/rest emit the spec spellings; build() warns (since 2026-10-18) about a non-absolute or plaintext interface URL and a listener whose binding the card omits. Whether the URL is reachable behind proxies is the deployer's.

entries.requirement: URLs **MAY** be reused if multiple transports are available at the same endpoint
entries.notes: No uniqueness constraint on interface URLs.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST: 1. Parse `supportedInterfaces` if present, and select the first supported transport
entries.notes: from_card applies no binding preference (it passed ClientConfig::default().preferred_bindings = ["JSONRPC"] until 2026-10-12, so a card listing [HTTP+JSON, JSONRPC] got JSONRPC). Among interfaces for protocol major 1 the card's order decides, and build() moves past one it cannot construct, which is what 'first supported' requires. from_card_preferring ranks bindings only when the caller asks it to.

entries.requirement: 2. Prefer earlier entries in the ordered list when multiple options are supported
entries.notes: from_card keeps the card's order, earlier entries first, with the rest as build() fallbacks in that order. from_card_preferring lets a caller who explicitly ranks bindings override the agent's order (a2a-go parity); card order then breaks ties within a rank.

entries.requirement: 3. Use the correct URL for the selected transport
entries.notes: Endpoint taken from the selected AgentInterface; fallback moves endpoint and binding together.

entries.requirement: 4. Set the `tenant` field in every request message to exactly the value declared in the selected `AgentInterface` entry (omit the field if `tenant` is not set in that entry)
entries.notes: Per-request params.tenant overrides the card value (user choice). gRPC/WS round-trip not covered by the e2e test.

entries.requirement: Agent Cards **MAY** be digitally signed using JSON Web Signature (JWS)
entries.notes: ES256 and EdDSA signers (signing feature).

entries.requirement: Before signing, the Agent Card content **MUST** be canonicalized using the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) as defined in RFC 8785.
entries.notes: JCS itself is implemented and vector-tested; see 2012/2016 for the pre-canonicalization default-stripping it is fed without.

entries.requirement: Before canonicalization, the JSON representation **MUST** respect Protocol Buffer field presence semantics as defined in Section 5.7.
entries.notes: signing::presence::prune applies protobuf field presence from a table the test checks against the vendored proto.

entries.requirement: Optional fields not explicitly set **MUST** be omitted from the JSON object
entries.notes: `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` on streaming/pushNotifications/extendedAgentCard/documentationUrl/iconUrl; no test asserts absence in canonical bytes.

entries.requirement: Optional fields explicitly set to defaults **MUST** be included in the JSON object
entries.notes: Option<bool> Some(false) serializes `false`; no test pins the spec example's `"pushNotifications":false,"streaming":false` in canonical output. The gRPC card conversion keeps an explicitly set empty iconUrl or documentationUrl (both `optional string` in a2a.proto) since 2026-10-13; it mapped Some("") to None both ways, so a card read over gRPC lost what a signature over the JSON card had covered.

entries.requirement: Required fields: Fields marked with `REQUIRED` **MUST** always be present, even if the field value matches the default.
entries.notes: name/description/version are String and supportedInterfaces/defaultInput/OutputModes/skills/tags are Vec with no skip_serializing_if, so always present; no test asserts e.g. `"description":""` / `"skills":[]` survive canonicalization.

entries.requirement: Default values: Fields with default values **MUST** be omitted unless the field is marked as `REQUIRED` or has the `optional` keyword.
test_evidence: itk/interop/card_signature_interop.py implicit fields at their defaults
entries.notes: Fixed; interop with the official Python SDK proven both ways (itk/interop/card_signature_interop.py).

entries.requirement: (example table) `extensions`: [] - repeated field (not REQUIRED) with empty array → **omit**; expected canonical {"capabilities":{"pushNotifications":false,"streaming":false},"description":"","name":"Example Agent","skills":[]}
entries.notes: A received `"extensions": []` deserializes to Some(vec![]) and is re-serialized as `"extensions":[]`, so the spec's own worked example canonicalizes differently from the documented output; no test runs the §8.4.1 example.

entries.requirement: The `signatures` field itself **MUST** be excluded from the content being signed to avoid circular dependencies.
The protected header **MUST** include: `alg`
The protected header **MUST** include: ... `kid`: Key ID for identifying the signing key
entries.notes: sign_card_es256/sign_card_ed25519 take the kid as &str. The deprecated sign_agent_card(_ed25519) still accept None until removal (STABILITY.md section 3).

entries.requirement: `typ`: **SHOULD** be set to "JOSE" for JWS
entries.notes: Protected header built as `json!({"alg": "ES256"})` (+kid); `typ` is never emitted by either signer.

entries.requirement: The protected header **MAY** include: `jku`
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-14 sign_card_es256_with_jku and sign_card_ed25519_with_jku put jku in the protected header, covered by the signature, and refuse one that is not https:// (RFC 7515 §4.1.2); signature_header reads jku from any signer. This SDK's verification never follows jku (§8.4.3 line 2122). Before: signers took no jku parameter.

entries.requirement: Clients verifying Agent Card signatures MUST: 1. Extract the signature from the `signatures` array
entries.notes: verify_card_with_jwks iterates card.signatures; verify_card_json_with_jwks reads them from the card as received.

entries.requirement: 2. Retrieve the public key using the `kid` and `jku` (or from a trusted key store)
entries.notes: The 'from a trusted key store' branch is what is implemented and tested: kid-based lookup in a caller-supplied JWKS. jku is decoded but never followed, deliberately: following a card's own jku would let the card name the key that vouches for it, and fetch_jwks takes a caller-trusted URL instead. Reclassified PARTIAL to TESTED on 2026-10-14 (audit register, the §8.4.3 row, approved).

entries.requirement: 3. Remove properties with default values from the received Agent Card
test_evidence: itk/interop/card_signature_interop.py implicit fields at their defaults
entries.notes: Removed from the card as received: verify_card_json_with_jwks, and the client fetch with signature keys, prune the JSON the peer served (canonicalize_card_json), leaving a field this SDK does not model in place. Until 2026-10-14 every path pruned the typed card's re-serialization, which had already dropped such fields (audit register R31). verify_card_with_jwks still verifies a card as this SDK models it. Removing the prune survived every test in the types crate until a_received_cards_defaults_are_dropped_before_canonicalizing.

entries.requirement: 4. Exclude the `signatures` field
5. Canonicalize the resulting JSON using RFC 8785
6. Verify the signature against the canonicalized payload
entries.notes: The signature is JWS (RFC 7515), whose §4.1.11 makes a JWS naming in crit an extension the recipient does not understand invalid. This verifier understands none, so since 2026-10-13 any crit, in the protected header or the unprotected one (where it may not appear), is refused; it was ignored, and a signature with crit ["exp"] verified forever.

entries.requirement: Clients **SHOULD** verify at least one signature before trusting an Agent Card
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: card discovery verifies signatures once keys are supplied (with_signature_keys, with_require_signature, from_signed_card) and refuses a card whose signatures were stripped. Which keys to trust stays the application's.

entries.requirement: Public keys **SHOULD** be retrieved over secure channels (HTTPS)
entries.notes: https:// or loopback http:// only.

entries.requirement: Clients **MAY** maintain a trusted key store for known agent providers
entries.notes: Caller-supplied Jwks.

entries.requirement: Expired or revoked keys **MUST NOT** be used for verification
entries.notes: Documented as the caller's obligation; no expiry/revocation check in the SDK (revocation only by removal from the JWKS).

entries.requirement: Multiple signatures **MAY** be present to support key rotation
Servers and clients **SHOULD** use standard HTTP caching mechanisms to reduce unnecessary network overhead.
entries.notes: Server: the public card is cacheable on JSON-RPC, REST and axum (Cache-Control max-age, ETag), the extended card revalidates (private, no-cache, Vary: Authorization, ETag). Client: since 2026-10-15 CachingCardResolver is an RFC 9111 private cache of the public card: a fresh card is returned without a request, a stale one is revalidated with If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since (details in 2225). resolve_agent_card, fetch_card_from_url and their _with_options / _with_path variants are one-shot free functions with no state to keep a cache in; their rustdoc says they are uncached and points to CachingCardResolver, the SDK's caching mechanism. Counted as met on that reading: a caller that fetches a card repeatedly has the cache to use. Server impl_evidence re-cited 2026-10-15 to the lines that set the headers; the axum lines cited before had moved.

entries.requirement: Agent Card HTTP endpoints **SHOULD** include a `Cache-Control` response header with a `max-age` directive appropriate for the agent's expected update frequency
entries.notes: JSON-RPC, REST and (since 2026-10-11) the axum router serve the public card with Cache-Control: public, max-age from StaticAgentCardHandler. Since 2026-10-14 the max-age is DispatchConfig::with_agent_card_max_age (default 3600, now pinned by the_axum_agent_card_is_cacheable_like_the_rest_one); the dispatchers had built their handlers with the default and exposed no way to set it, so the "appropriate for the agent's expected update frequency" half of the line was not met. The axum test fails without the 2026-10-11 fix (no cache-control).

entries.requirement: Agent Card HTTP endpoints **SHOULD** include an `ETag` response header derived from the Agent Card's `version` field or a hash of the card content
entries.notes: Content-hash ETag (and Last-Modified) on all three HTTP card routes; If-None-Match answers 304. The axum route had neither until 2026-10-11. The hash is over the card with its maps' keys sorted (card_body_and_etag), since 2026-10-13. It was over the serialization, whose HashMap fields (securitySchemes, a requirement's schemes, OAuth scopes) come out in an order each map draws at random: the same card had another ETag on each replica, after each restart, and on each request of a dynamic handler building its card, so revalidation returned 200. Shown 8 ETags in 8 parses before the fix. Since 2026-10-13 a 304 answers only a GET or HEAD, every If-None-Match line is read (RFC 9110 §13.1.2, §5.3), and HEAD on the card is served on JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON and axum; before, any method got a 304, only the first line was read, and a HEAD was refused or not found.

entries.requirement: Agent Card HTTP endpoints **MAY** include a `Last-Modified` response header
entries.notes: Static handler: set to handler construction time (changes on every restart); If-Modified-Since compared by exact string equality (caching.rs:159), and ignored when If-None-Match is present, readable or not, or the method is not GET or HEAD (RFC 9110 §13.1.3; until 2026-10-13 an unreadable If-None-Match fell through to it). Dynamic handler: sends none since 2026-10-13. It had stamped the current second on every request, claiming the card changed at each one; a card produced per request has no modification date (RFC 9110 §8.8.2.1), so it now ignores If-Modified-Since (§13.1.3) and revalidates by ETag alone.

entries.requirement: Clients **SHOULD** honor HTTP caching semantics as defined in RFC 9111 when fetching Agent Cards
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-15 CachingCardResolver honours freshness (RFC 9111 §4.2): a stored card is returned without a request while its age is less than its freshness lifetime, the lifetime being max-age, else Expires minus Date (§4.2.1; an invalid Expires is in the past, §5.3), and the age max(apparent_age, Age + response_delay) plus the time since arrival (§4.2.3). A stale card is revalidated with its validators, which a 304 replaces (§4.3.4, since 2026-10-13); the 304's own Cache-Control / Expires set the new freshness. no-cache and Vary: * revalidate on every resolve (§5.2.2.4, §4.1); no-store is not stored (§5.2.2.5, since 2026-10-12); a card is kept only with a validator or a lifetime. s-maxage and proxy-revalidate are shared-cache only; private permits this cache; must-revalidate holds because a stale card is never returned. Vary naming fields needs no handling: one resolver sends the same request fields on every fetch, and with_options (since 2026-10-15) starts a new cache, so a card stored under one credential is never returned for another; the resolver fetches the public card only, and an extended card (Vary: Authorization) is installed by the caller. with_always_revalidate(true) restores revalidation on every resolve. Deliberate simplifications, documented in discovery/freshness.rs: a 304 without Cache-Control or Expires leaves the card stale (§4.3.4 would carry the stored ones over; RFC 9110 §15.4.5 requires the 304 to send them), a qualified no-cache="field" counts as unqualified, and there is no heuristic freshness except the opt-in default (2227). resolve_agent_card / fetch_card_from_url keep no cache (see 2215).

entries.requirement: When a cached Agent Card has expired, clients **SHOULD** use conditional requests (`If-None-Match` with the stored `ETag`, or `If-Modified-Since`)
entries.notes: CachingCardResolver revalidates on every resolve with If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since from the cached response; a server that answers 304 only to a request carrying both validators sees them on the second fetch. Shown to fail with the If-None-Match header removed.

entries.requirement: When the server does not include caching headers, clients **MAY** apply an implementation-specific default cache duration
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-15, opt-in: CachingCardResolver::with_default_freshness(lifetime) gives a card whose response has no max-age and no Expires that freshness lifetime (RFC 9111 §4.2.2 heuristic freshness), less any Age it arrived with, capped at 2^31 s. It never applies to a no-cache, Vary: * or no-store response, and is off by default, so without it such a card is revalidated on every resolve.

entries.requirement: Content-Type: `application/json` for requests and responses
entries.notes: Server emits `application/json` (JSON_CONTENT_TYPE) on every JSON-RPC response and accepts application/json or application/a2a+json on ingress; client sends application/json. A refused Content-Type is answered with the request's id since 2026-10-13 (it answered null). Since 2026-10-13 the request's Content-Type is read as a media type (RFC 9110 §8.3.1): the type and subtype before any parameter, case-insensitively. It was compared by prefix, case-sensitively, so Application/JSON was refused and application/json-rpc accepted.

entries.requirement: Streaming: Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`); SendStreamingMessage response HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/event-stream, each `data:` a JSON-RPC response echoing the request id
entries.notes: Frames are `id: <seq>\nevent: message\ndata: {jsonrpc,id,result}`; the extra `id:`/`event:` SSE fields are permitted by SSE and do not change the §9.4.2 data shape. Pre-stream errors are returned as plain application/json (deliberate, TCK-driven, jsonrpc/mod.rs:90-97).

entries.requirement: A2A service parameters ... MUST be transmitted using standard HTTP request headers
entries.notes: Server reads A2A-Version/A2A-Extensions/auth from HTTP headers and forwards all headers to the handler; client sets A2A-Version and interceptor-supplied headers as HTTP headers.

entries.requirement: Service parameter names MUST be transmitted as HTTP header fields
entries.notes: Header names are lower-cased by hyper, which satisfies the RFC 7230 case-insensitivity note on line 2247.

entries.requirement: Multiple values for the same service parameter (e.g., A2A-Extensions) SHOULD be comma-separated in a single header field
entries.notes: The client sends what ClientBuilder::with_extensions asks for as one comma-joined field (extensions::header_value), and extra_headers, a HashMap, holds one field per name; server splits on commas and echoes activated extensions as one comma-joined field. A peer that sends A2A-Extensions as several header lines is read as one field, the lines joined in order with ", " (dispatch::header_fields, RFC 9110 §5.3), on the JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON, axum, gRPC and WebSocket bindings, and the JSON-RPC echo reads the same value. Until 2026-10-13 each binding kept the last line and the JSON-RPC echo the first.

entries.requirement: All JSON-RPC requests MUST follow the standard JSON-RPC 2.0 format
entries.notes: `jsonrpc` must be exactly "2.0"; non-JSON answers -32700, JSON that is not a Request answers -32600. Client always emits `jsonrpc:"2.0"`, PascalCase method, params object. A request refused for its A2A-Version or Content-Type is answered with its own id, and a batch with one error per request, since 2026-10-13: both were refused before the body was read, so the response id was null (JSON-RPC 2.0 §5: the id MUST be the request's, null only when it cannot be detected) and a batch got one object. A batch beyond max_batch_size, and a body that is not JSON or over the size limit, still get one null-id refusal. Also since 2026-10-13, over HTTP and WebSocket: an id that is not a string, a number or null (JSON-RPC 2.0 §4) is -32600 with a null id, where it was run and echoed; an omitted params (§4.2: MAY be omitted) is read as {}, where it was "missing params"; a stream inside a batch is UnsupportedOperation (-32004), where it was -32602. Since 2026-10-14 a notification (no id member) is run and not answered (§4.1, audit register R21): 204 No Content alone or when a batch holds only notifications, left out of a batch's array, no WebSocket frame, and no answer when refused on its headers; a streaming method sent as one is refused rather than run. Until then each was answered with a null id.

entries.requirement: SubscribeToTask returns UnsupportedOperationError if the task is in a terminal state
entries.notes: Shared handler path, so it holds for JSON-RPC, REST, gRPC, WebSocket and SLIMRPC; wire mapping is -32004 / 400 / FAILED_PRECONDITION (SLIMRPC: UNIMPLEMENTED, see 3017).

entries.requirement: Error Details: Mapped to error.data (array of objects, each containing a @type key, using ProtoJSON Any representation)
entries.notes: Every JSON-RPC error object comes from sse::jsonrpc_error_from, on HTTP responses, SSE frames and WebSocket messages alike: error.data is the array sse::error_details builds, ErrorInfo when the code has an A2A reason (and RetryInfo for a rate limit), then A2aError.data as a further typed detail (as it is when it names its @type, otherwise a google.protobuf.Struct, where the streamLagged marker lives). Since 2026-10-14 (audit register R19) the Struct is written as ProtoJSON writes an Any holding a special-cased well-known type, {"@type": ..., "value": {...}}; it was flat, its fields beside @type. Until 2026-10-10 the SSE frame copied A2aError.data through as a bare object; until 2026-10-11 (ef31df91) the HTTP response dropped A2aError.data and the WebSocket binding sent no data. Clients recognise the marker in every shape: top-level data, a flat Struct detail (older servers, a2a-go) and the Any form (A2aError::lag_marker; the REST client's error_frame::struct_detail).

entries.requirement: Standard JSON-RPC error codes -32700/-32600/-32601/-32602/-32603
entries.notes: The codes match the table. The messages are free text such as "Parse error: ..." and "invalid params: ...", not the table's "Standard Message" column. That column is informational, so this is not a violation.

entries.requirement: A2A-specific errors use codes in the range -32001 to -32099 (§5.4 mapping)
entries.notes: A2A errors use -32001..-32099 on every JSON-RPC surface. The WebSocket binding's -32000 (mid-stream and over-capacity) is gone: mid-stream errors keep their own code, and over-capacity is sent as an overload (-32603), as the JSON-RPC HTTP binding sends one.

entries.requirement: Each object in the data array MUST include a @type key that identifies the object's type
entries.notes: Unary, pre-stream and mid-stream errors carry the same array (sse::error_details), and every element has @type: ErrorInfo, RetryInfo for a rate limit, then A2aError.data as itself when it names its @type or as a google.protobuf.Struct. The stream test asserts every element has @type.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD use well-known types such as google.rpc.ErrorInfo ..., or google.rpc.BadRequest to attach structured data to validation errors
entries.notes: A2A errors carry ErrorInfo. Params that do not deserialize answer InvalidParams with a google.rpc.BadRequest naming the field path, on JSON-RPC (HTTP and WebSocket), HTTP+JSON and gRPC (from ConvertError's field).

entries.requirement: Additional error context MAY be included as further objects in the data array
entries.notes: A2aError::data reaches the client as a further detail (a Struct, or as is when it names its @type) on JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON unary responses, on both bindings' stream frames, and on WebSocket. Since 2026-10-13 gRPC carries it too, unary and stream: a BadRequest as google.rpc.BadRequest, other data as a google.protobuf.Struct Any (dispatch/grpc/details.rs). SLIMRPC carries the message text only.

entries.requirement: A2A service parameters ... MUST be transmitted using gRPC metadata (headers)
entries.notes: Client puts a2a-version plus all interceptor headers into tonic metadata. The server copies ASCII metadata into the header map that the handler reads.

entries.requirement: Service parameter names MUST be transmitted as gRPC metadata keys
entries.notes: Binary (-bin) metadata is skipped on ingress (keys ending -bin are dropped). That is fine because A2A parameters are ASCII.

entries.requirement: Multiple values for the same service parameter SHOULD be comma-separated in a single metadata entry
entries.notes: The client sends one a2a-extensions entry, the comma-joined list ClientBuilder::with_extensions asks for (one entry per key: extra_headers is a HashMap). On ingress, repeated a2a-extensions entries are one field, joined in order with ", " (extract_metadata through dispatch::header_fields); until 2026-10-13 they collapsed to the last one.

entries.requirement: Implementations MUST extract A2A service parameters from gRPC metadata for processing
entries.notes: All 11 RPCs call validated_metadata(request.metadata(), ..) and pass the headers to the handler.

entries.requirement: Servers SHOULD validate required service parameters (e.g., A2A-Version) from metadata
entries.notes: Absent and empty values, and any version but 1.0 with some patch, are rejected with FAILED_PRECONDITION plus ErrorInfo VERSION_NOT_SUPPORTED under the default require_version_header=true.

entries.requirement: For A2A-specific errors, implementations MUST include a google.rpc.ErrorInfo message in the status.details array with reason (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE) and domain "a2a-protocol.org"
entries.notes: Unary, pre-stream and mid-stream errors carry ErrorInfo through tonic_types: since 2026-10-13 reader_to_native_stream sends a stream's error through server_error_to_status as a unary call's. It was Status::internal("event queue error"), which lost the message and the streamLagged marker.

entries.requirement: Content-Type: application/a2a+json SHOULD be used for requests and responses
test_evidence: scripts/go_sdk_interop.sh Go SDK interop: both directions passed
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-15 (maintainer decision) the server answers application/a2a+json whenever the request states no preference: no Accept, only wildcards or unrelated types, with or without an application/json body; before, those got application/json, so the spec examples at lines 2835-2836 and 2921-2922 were not matched by default. Accept still decides when it names either JSON type, and an a2a+json body is answered in kind. Remaining, why PARTIAL/low: a request whose Accept asks only for text/event-stream is answered application/json (only an error is JSON there). Released a2a-go v2.6.0 sends exactly that on SendStreamingMessage and SubscribeToTask (a2aclient/rest.go:115) and decodes an error body only under application/json (internal/rest/rest.go:276), so a refused Go stream would lose its error identity; read in the v2.6.0 source 2026-10-15, and go_sdk_interop.sh passes both directions on every binding with the rule. The report asking a2a-go to read a2a+json errors is docs/upstream/a2a-go-a2a-json-errors-report.md (held). Since 2026-10-13 the request's Content-Type is read as a media type (RFC 9110 §8.3.1), a negotiated response names Accept and Content-Type in Vary (RFC 9110 §12.5.5), and every Accept line is read (§5.3).

entries.requirement: Content-Type: application/a2a+json SHOULD be used for requests
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-14 (audit register R50) the REST client labels a request body application/a2a+json, sends no Content-Type on a GET or DELETE (no body), and asks Accept: application/a2a+json, application/json on a non-streaming call. Until then every request, bodiless ones included, was labelled application/json, for interop: a2a-java 1.3.0.Final's REST server refuses any other type (A2AServerRoutes.validateContentType, read from the jar's bytecode with javap, 2026-10-10). a2a-java accepts application/a2a+json from 1.4.0.Final (pin-freshness run 38299384752; this repository's a2a-tck a2a_media_type_accepted on REST), which the ITK pins; an older a2a-java server is reached over JSON-RPC (upgrading guide). a2a-go v2.5.0 and a2a-sdk 1.1.4 servers do not check the request type, and this server accepts both.

entries.requirement: A2A service parameters ... MUST be transmitted using standard HTTP request headers
entries.notes: RestDispatcher validates A2A-Version and forwards headers. The axum adapter (A2aRouter) forwards headers and validates A2A-Version as RestDispatcher does (axum_adapter.rs:212, validate_a2a_request).

entries.requirement: Service parameter names MUST be transmitted as HTTP header fields
Multiple values for the same service parameter SHOULD be comma-separated in a single header field
entries.notes: Same as 2248. Repeated header lines collapse to the last one in rest/response.rs:21.

entries.requirement: REST URL patterns: POST /message:send, /message:stream; GET /tasks/{id}; GET /tasks; POST /tasks/{id}:cancel; POST /tasks/{id}:subscribe; push-config CRUD under /tasks/{id}/pushNotificationConfigs[/{configId}]; GET /extendedAgentCard
entries.notes: Every route exists on server and client, plus tolerated aliases (GET :subscribe, /tasks/{id}/cancel, singular pushNotificationConfig, POST .../{id}/delete). The client percent-encodes path ids; since 2026-10-12 the REST dispatcher decodes task and config ids (and the tenant) after routing, with + literal as RFC 3986 says, and the axum router routes on the raw path before decoding, so an id with a space, +, : or / round-trips on both. Shown to fail with the decoder disabled. Since 2026-10-13 the REST dispatcher's traversal guard refuses a dot segment (`.` or `..`, RFC 3986 §3.3, raw or encoded at any depth, `\` read as a separator), not every `..`: an id such as `v1..prod`, which the other bindings serve, answered 400 on every route.

entries.requirement: HTTP methods that do not support request bodies (GET, DELETE) MUST transmit operation request parameters as path parameters or query parameters
entries.notes: Client sends an empty body on GET/DELETE and puts the leftover params in the query. Server reads GetTask historyLength and ListTasks filters from the query, and the tenant from `?tenant=` when there is no path prefix. The axum router (A2aRouter) does the same since 2026-10-13: until then it read neither GetTask's historyLength nor any GET or DELETE route's `?tenant=`, so `GET /tasks/{id}?historyLength=0` returned the whole history.

entries.requirement: Query parameter names MUST use camelCase to match the JSON serialization of Protocol Buffer field names
entries.notes: Keys used: contextId, status, pageSize, pageToken, statusTimestampAfter, includeArtifacts, historyLength, tenant. A malformed value such as `status=BOGUS` or `pageSize=abc` is refused with InvalidParams (2026-10-13); until then it was dropped and an unfiltered list returned.

entries.requirement: Booleans lowercase strings; Numbers decimal strings; Enums string values (status=TASK_STATE_WORKING); Datetimes ISO 8601
entries.notes: Server also accepts `1` for true and legacy lowercase enum aliases. Both are lenient extensions.

entries.requirement: Repeated Fields: multiple values MAY be passed by repeating the parameter name or as comma-separated values
entries.notes: No v1.0 GET or DELETE request has a repeated field, so this has no wire effect today. Since 2026-10-15 the client sends an array by repeating the parameter, one per element (the first form the MAY names); it JSON-encoded the array (ids=%5B1%2C2%5D), which matched neither form. The server has no repeated field to read: parse_query_param returns a parameter's first occurrence, which is right for the single-valued fields every v1.0 route takes. Counted as SUPPORTED on that reading: what this SDK sends follows the MAY, and there is nothing for it to receive.

entries.requirement: Nested Objects: Not supported in query parameters; operations requiring nested objects MUST use POST with a request body
entries.notes: Every operation with nested fields (SendMessage, CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig, CancelTask metadata) is routed POST, so the MUST holds by route design. build_query_string would still JSON-encode a nested object into the query instead of refusing it (test pins this), which is latent rather than wire-observable.

entries.requirement: All query parameter values MUST be properly URL-encoded per RFC 3986
entries.notes: Client encodes everything except RFC 3986 unreserved chars. Server percent-decodes values (and `+` as space). Query keys are compared undecoded, which is harmless for the camelCase ASCII keys.

entries.requirement: Error Code mapped to the HTTP status code and the error.code field; message to error.message; details to error.details
entries.notes: Body shape `{error:{code,status,message,details}}` matches the spec example at lines 2924-2941, except that ErrorInfo.metadata is never populated (it is optional). The axum router's own refusals, made before any A2A handler runs, take the same shape since 2026-10-14: a method a route does not take (405, Allow kept), a body over the cap (413), one not received in time (408), an unreadable one (400). They were axum's plain text, or no body for 405. An unknown path outside the A2A routes stays the composing app's to answer.

entries.requirement: Each object in the details array MUST include a @type key that identifies the object's type
entries.notes: Unary and stream REST error bodies both take sse::error_details: ErrorInfo (RetryInfo for a rate limit), then A2aError.data as itself when it names its @type or as a google.protobuf.Struct; every element has @type.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD use well-known types such as google.rpc.BadRequest to attach structured data to validation errors
entries.notes: A request body that is valid JSON of the wrong shape answers 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT with a google.rpc.BadRequest detail whose fieldViolation names the path (e.g. message.parts[0].text), on RestDispatcher (send, cancel, subscribe, create push config) and the axum router (send, create push config). Malformed JSON stays a plain 400. Not covered: query-string parameter errors and the JSON-RPC binding's -32602.

entries.requirement: Additional error context MAY be included as further objects in the details array
entries.notes: A2aError.data goes as a further object after ErrorInfo in a unary REST error's details and in a stream error frame's (sse::error_details): as itself when it names its @type, otherwise as a google.protobuf.Struct. Until 2026-10-11 (ef31df91) the unary body dropped it.

entries.requirement: implementations MUST include a google.rpc.ErrorInfo object in the details array for A2A-specific errors with @type, reason, domain
entries.notes: ContentTypeNotSupportedError now goes through server_error_to_response with its ErrorInfo on REST and axum.

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD avoid re-ordering events
entries.notes: A single ordered per-task queue drives SSE, gRPC, WebSocket and SLIMRPC streams. REST frames are bare StreamResponse objects as the §11.7 example requires.

entries.requirement: MAY optionally resend a final Task snapshot before closing
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-15, opt-in (HandlerLimits::with_final_task_snapshot): a send stream and a SubscribeToTask stream send the task once more, as a Task without a position, after the terminal state and before closing, on every binding (they all stream the same reader). It is read once the queue's consumer has stored the terminal event (the applied mark), waiting at most subscribe_replay_catchup, and is sent only when that read is exact and the stored task is terminal: no snapshot rather than an older one. A send stream's snapshot is trimmed to the history the request asked for, as its first Task is. Off by default, so the stream still ends right after the terminal event unless asked.

entries.requirement: implementers MAY create custom protocol bindings
entries.notes: Two custom bindings: WebSocket (https://a2a-rust.com/bindings/websocket/v1) and SLIMRPC (https://a2a-protocol.org/bindings/experimental-slimrpc/v1).

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST comply with all requirements defined in Section 5
entries.notes: SLIMRPC sends PushNotificationNotSupported and UnsupportedOperation as UNIMPLEMENTED where A2A §5.4's gRPC column says FAILED_PRECONDITION. This is the SLIMRPC spec's own §6.1 'canonical mapping' (a MUST), which the binding now follows exactly; the conflict is between the two specifications, not an implementation defect, and is left PARTIAL until upstream resolves it. The stale 'identical to dispatch/grpc' comment was rewritten. Reclassified PARTIAL to TESTED on 2026-10-14 (audit register, the §12/§5.4 row, approved): the text asks for an equivalent mapping that preserves each error's meaning, which the SLIMRPC mapping does, not for the gRPC column itself. The conflict between the two specifications is for upstream; a report is drafted for the maintainer, not filed.

entries.requirement: Custom protocol bindings MUST: 1. Implement All Core Operations
entries.notes: Both bindings route all 11 v1.0 methods to the shared RequestHandler. WebSocket also accepts the v0.3 alias `message/stream` (websocket.rs:883). The module rustdoc (websocket.rs:20-23) says v0.3 names are rejected, while the book (dispatchers.md:225-229) documents the alias; the alias is untested (ws_legacy_method_names_rejected covers only message/send, tasks/list, tasks/get).

entries.requirement: 2. Preserve Data Model: Use data structures functionally equivalent to those defined in Section 4
entries.notes: WebSocket reuses the JSON-RPC ProtoJSON types. SLIMRPC uses the canonical lf.a2a.v1 protobuf messages.

entries.requirement: 3. Maintain Semantics: Ensure operations behave consistently with the abstract operation definitions
entries.notes: Same handler, so the semantics match. Deviations: WebSocket ends every stream with a synthetic success frame `{"result":{"status":"stream_complete"}}` that is not a StreamResponse (documented). SLIMRPC accepts a missing a2a-version (methods/mod.rs:96 `validate_version_metadata(&headers, false)`), unlike the strict default of the other bindings. Its rationale comment ("the gRPC binding already made exactly this trade") is stale, since gRPC now enforces it (helpers.rs:42-51).

entries.requirement: 4. Document Completely: Provide comprehensive documentation of the binding specification
entries.notes: WebSocket now has a binding specification (book/src/bindings/websocket.md): connection, service parameters, messages, data types, streaming, errors, authentication, security, differences from JSON-RPC over HTTP. SLIMRPC follows the vendored upstream spec. The page's wire claims are pinned by websocket_binding_spec.rs (handshake refusal and query fallback, refusal codes and ErrorInfo, stream frames and marker), which passed against the page as written.

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST provide clear mappings for: Protocol Buffer Types, Timestamps, Binary Data, Enumerations
entries.notes: WebSocket spec §3 'Data types' states the ProtoJSON mappings: lowerCamelCase names, enum names as strings, RFC 3339 UTC timestamps, base64 bytes, Struct as JSON object; binary frames refused. SLIMRPC is protobuf on the wire.

entries.requirement: custom protocol bindings MUST document how service parameters are transmitted ... MUST address: Transmission Mechanism, Value Constraints, Reserved Names, Fallback Strategy
entries.notes: WebSocket spec §2 covers transmission, value constraints, reserved names (:path) and fallback (A2A-Version query parameter only). The page's wire claims are pinned by websocket_binding_spec.rs (handshake refusal and query fallback, refusal codes and ErrorInfo, stream frames and marker), which passed against the page as written.

entries.requirement: Transmission Mechanism (SLIMRPC: service parameter keys are case-insensitive in metadata, spec/slimrpc_v1/slimrpc.md:63)
entries.notes: a2a_headers lowercases every key after filtering the transport keys, so the handler's lowercase lookups (authorization, a2a-extensions, a2a-version, tenant headers) see a capitalised key; keys differing only in case are joined with ', '. Until 2026-10-10 keys kept the peer's case and were ignored. Since 2026-10-13 it also drops a key beginning with ':' (`:peer-addr`, `:path`), which names what a server records rather than what a caller sends; until then a caller's `:peer-addr` reached CallContext::peer_addr.

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST: 1. Map Standard Errors: Provide mappings for all A2A-specific error types
2. Preserve Error Information: Ensure error details are accessible to clients
entries.notes: WebSocket: unary, mid-stream and over-capacity errors now carry their own code and the same typed data array as the JSON-RPC HTTP binding (ErrorInfo, RetryInfo, BadRequest, A2aError::data); mid-stream errors keep their A2A code and the streamLagged marker instead of -32000. A SLIMRPC multicast member that falls behind is handed the typed streamLagged error since 2026-10-14 (audit register R66); it was a Transport error carrying only text. Remaining (why PARTIAL/low): SLIMRPC keeps identity through its TypeNameError: message prefix but carries no details. Its spec lists optional details (§6.2) without an encoding, and agntcy-slim-rpc sends an error's code and message only: its error send (send_error_to in 3.4.1, which the binding uses since R13 and is the latest release, rpc_session.rs:152-174; send_error_for_rpc in 2.3.0 before it) drops details, and the receiver builds the error with none (channel.rs:704-714; both read 2026-10-15). Upstream report: docs/upstream/slimrpc-a2a-error-mapping-report.md (held).

entries.requirement: 3. Use Appropriate Codes: Map to protocol-native error codes where applicable
entries.notes: The binding follows the SLIMRPC spec's §6.1 table row by row (ParseError INTERNAL, ContentTypeNotSupported/Push/UnsupportedOperation UNIMPLEMENTED) and A2A §5.4's gRPC code for the three errors the table omits (FAILED_PRECONDITION). The table's UNKNOWN row has no case to apply to: every ServerError converts to an A2A code. Where the SLIMRPC table and A2A §5.4's gRPC column disagree (Push, UnsupportedOperation), the binding's own table is followed; see the §12 entry at line 2977.

entries.requirement: 4. Document Error Format: Specify the structure of error responses
entries.notes: WebSocket spec §1 and §5 document the handshake error body and the JSON-RPC error object with its typed data array, with a code table for every A2A error. The page's wire claims are pinned by websocket_binding_spec.rs (handshake refusal and query fallback, refusal codes and ErrorInfo, stream frames and marker), which passed against the page as written.

entries.requirement: Define Stream Mechanism; Event Ordering; Reconnection; Stream Termination
entries.notes: WebSocket spec §4: mechanism (frames carrying the request id), ordering (per stream in production order; streams on one connection interleave), reconnection (none; resubscribe, first event is the snapshot), termination (stream_complete marker, or an error frame). The page's wire claims are pinned by websocket_binding_spec.rs (handshake refusal and query fallback, refusal codes and ErrorInfo, stream frames and marker), which passed against the page as written. Reconnection held only without a Last-Event-ID on the upgrade request: the upgrade's headers reach every call on the connection, so until 2026-10-14 one made every SubscribeToTask replay the event log from it. The header is now dropped at the handshake.

entries.requirement: If streaming is not supported, the binding MUST clearly document this limitation in the Agent Card
entries.notes: Both custom bindings support streaming.

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST: Support Standard Schemes; Document Integration; Handle Challenges; Maintain Security
entries.notes: Both custom bindings support the card's schemes, document how credentials travel, and say how a challenge is communicated. WebSocket (binding spec §6): credentials on the upgrade headers, checked by the interceptors on every request. Since 2026-10-15 a refused credential is -32600 carrying a google.rpc.ErrorInfo from a2a-rust.com, UNAUTHENTICATED with the challenge as www-authenticate metadata (as the gRPC binding's status carries it) or PERMISSION_DENIED, and the client reports the two as UnexpectedStatus 401/403, as on HTTP and gRPC, on a unary call and as a stream's first item. Until then the -32600 had no data: the challenge was dropped, and nothing told the refusal from a malformed request (the binding and e2e tests fail without the change, on the server half and on the client half). A credential is fixed for the connection, so recovering means a new one; browsers cannot set Authorization on the upgrade, and the documented route is a gateway. SLIMRPC authenticates at the transport (JWT, SPIFFE) and maps refusals to UNAUTHENTICATED/PERMISSION_DENIED, the challenge ending the UNAUTHENTICATED message, as SLIMRPC errors carry no details on the wire.

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST be declared in the Agent Card (URI transport identifier + full endpoint URL) - WebSocket
entries.notes: WEBSOCKET_BINDING_URI and AgentInterface::new(url, uri) give the declaration; since 2026-10-18 the WebSocket listener warns when it starts if the static card does not declare it. The dispatcher never edits the card (a signed card cannot be edited).

entries.requirement: Custom bindings MUST be declared in the Agent Card (URI transport identifier + full endpoint URL) - SLIMRPC
entries.notes: server.agent_interface() builds the interface with the upstream URI. The application must still push it onto card.supported_interfaces (README example).

entries.requirement: Custom binding implementers SHOULD: Test Against Reference; Document Differences; Provide Examples; Test Edge Cases
entries.notes: WebSocket: examples and a differences table are in the binding spec (§3, §5, §8); TCK --equivalence compares it with the spec bindings; edge cases are tested in websocket.rs and websocket_*.rs. SLIMRPC is checked against upstream's spec and the official crate.

entries.requirement: Implementations MUST ensure appropriate scope limitation based on the authenticated caller's authorization boundaries. This applies to all operations that access or list tasks and other resources.
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: caller isolation is on by default with an authenticating interceptor (builder.rs build) and scopes every operation to the caller's partition. The earlier note cited a function name (in_caller_partition) that does not exist; it is enter_caller_partition.

entries.requirement: Servers MUST implement authorization checks on every A2A Protocol Operations request
entries.notes: SDK hook provided: every handler entry point (all 11 operations, all bindings incl. WebSocket per message) runs ServerInterceptorChain::before, and ServerInterceptor can return A2aError::permission_denied keyed on ctx.method()/caller_identity(). Nothing enforces that an authorizer is registered; a default build performs no authorization (the interceptor sees no task id, so per-resource checks cannot be written there; see 3092).

entries.requirement: Implementations MUST scope results to the caller's authorized access boundaries as defined by the agent's authorization model
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: results are scoped to the caller's partition by default once callers are identified; see §13.1 3075.

entries.requirement: Even when contextId or other filter parameters are not specified in requests, implementations MUST scope results to the caller's authorized access boundaries
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: a ListTasks with no filter returns only the caller's partition (the test lists with default params).

entries.requirement: Authorization models are agent-defined and MAY be based on: user identity, roles/groups, project/workspace, tenant boundaries, custom logic
entries.notes: MAY: multi-tenant model SUPPORTED (TenantResolver + TenantAware stores); user/role/project models only expressible as tenants or as method-level allow/deny in an interceptor; no resource-level hook. (Re-graded on 2026-10-10: a MAY takes SUPPORTED/NOT_SUPPORTED; the tenant model is supported, and the missing per-principal hook is the §13.1 entries at lines 3075-3093.) The user-identity model is now supported too: isolate_tasks_by_caller, the default with an authenticating interceptor since 2026-10-12.

entries.requirement: List Tasks: MUST only return tasks visible to the authenticated client according to the agent's authorization model
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: met by caller isolation; Bob lists none of Alice's tasks.

entries.requirement: Get Task: MUST verify the authenticated client has access to the requested task according to the agent's authorization model
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: GetTask for another caller's task is TaskNotFound, as for an unknown id.

entries.requirement: Task-related operations (Cancel, Subscribe, Push Notification Config): MUST verify the client has appropriate access rights according to the agent's authorization model
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: Cancel, Subscribe and the push-config operations on another caller's task are refused as not found; a webhook Bob registers lands in his own partition.

entries.requirement: Authorization checks MUST occur before any database queries or operations that could leak information about the existence of resources outside the caller's authorization scope
entries.notes: call.before() (interceptors) and resolve_tenant/isolatable run before any task_store access in every handler; out-of-partition tasks surface as TaskNotFound, indistinguishable from nonexistent. Caveat: the CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig taskId-empty check (push_config.rs:167) runs before interceptors but reads no store.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD document their authorization model and access control policies
entries.notes: Deployment documentation duty; the SDK documents its own (tenant-only) model in tenant_resolver.rs module docs and book/src/deployment/multi-tenancy.md. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: the spec leaves the authorization model to each agent. The SDK documents the model it enforces by default, caller isolation within a tenant (book/src/deployment/multi-tenancy.md); the earlier wording 'tenant-only' was stale.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST include authentication credentials in webhook requests as specified in PushNotificationConfig.authentication
entries.notes: The sender writes Authorization for Bearer and Basic (case-insensitive), as a2a-go v2.5.0 does. A config naming any other scheme is now refused at creation with InvalidParams, so no webhook is called without the credentials its config specifies. Until 2026-10-10 such a config was stored and delivered without credentials (a2a-go still does that). The sender's runtime drop remains for configs stored before. Since 2026-10-13 a token or credentials a header cannot carry (CR, LF or another control character) is InvalidParams at creation, inline or by CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig; it was stored and refused at every delivery.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement reasonable timeout values for webhook requests (recommended: 10-30 seconds)
entries.notes: Per-request timeout 10s, whole-delivery bound 30s by default, both configurable (HttpPushSender::with_timeout, HandlerLimits::with_push_delivery_timeout). The test that used to pin the two defaults contradicting each other now pins that they fit: every attempt starts, two finish.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement retry logic with exponential backoff for failed deliveries
entries.notes: 3 attempts, backoff [1s,2s] (doubling; schedule is an explicit list whose last entry repeats, not computed exponential). Retries 5xx/408/429/transport errors only. Caveat: under the default 5s handler bound a timed-out first attempt leaves no time for retries (see 3110).

entries.requirement: Agents MAY stop attempting delivery after a configured number of consecutive failures
entries.notes: Per-event max_attempts only; no cross-event circuit breaker that disables a config after N consecutive failed events.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD validate webhook URLs to prevent SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) attacks
entries.notes: Synchronous host check at config creation, DNS-resolve-all + IP pinning at delivery (http), cert validation defeats rebinding for https. Bypassable only by explicit HttpPushSender::allow_private_urls().
Also CGNAT, 0.0.0.0, IPv6 ULA, IPv4-mapped/NAT64 forms and inet_aton numeric encodings.

entries.requirement: Reject localhost and link-local addresses
entries.notes: localhost, *.local, *.internal hostnames and 169.254/16, fe80::/10 rejected.

entries.requirement: Implement URL allowlists where appropriate
entries.notes: Opt-in HttpPushSender::with_allowed_hosts: exact host match, ignoring case and port, no wildcards. Enforced at config creation (InvalidParams) and again at delivery before any connection. Custom senders can answer PushSender::allows_webhook_url (default true).

entries.requirement: Clients MUST validate webhook authenticity using the provided authentication credentials
entries.notes: No webhook receiver exists in the client crate (no 'webhook' in a2a-protocol-client/src). The server crate offers only push::webhook::notification_token() to extract the token; the receiver must validate it (and Authorization) itself.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD verify the task ID in the payload matches an expected task they created
entries.notes: No receiver-side helper; application duty.

entries.requirement: Clients MUST respond with HTTP 2xx status codes to acknowledge successful receipt
entries.notes: Receiver duty; the SDK sender side treats any 2xx (`resp.status().is_success()`) as delivered, consistent with this.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD process notifications idempotently, as duplicate deliveries may occur
entries.notes: Receiver duty; no SDK receiver.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD implement rate limiting to prevent webhook flooding
entries.notes: Receiver duty; no SDK receiver.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD use HTTPS endpoints for webhook URLs to ensure confidentiality
entries.notes: Client picks the URL; the A2A client does not warn on http:// push URLs and the server accepts both http and https, unless its push sender is set to https_only (since 2026-10-12).

entries.requirement: Webhook URLs SHOULD use HTTPS to protect payload confidentiality in transit
entries.notes: HTTPS delivery supported (tls-rustls feature, on by default via sdk) and tested over real TLS. Since 2026-10-12 opt-in HttpPushSender::https_only() refuses an http:// webhook at config creation (InvalidParams naming the reason, via PushSender::requires_https) and again at delivery before any connection, as the opt-in allowlist (line 3116) does for hosts. Off by default: plain http is still accepted unless a deployment sets it. Before: no option enforced https.

entries.requirement: Authentication tokens in PushNotificationConfig SHOULD be treated as secrets and rotated periodically
entries.notes: Secret handling (Debug redaction, origin-only URL logging) tested; rotation is an application duty (re-create config). The background delivery's failure and timeout WARNs logged the whole webhook URL, path and query included, until 2026-10-14 (audit register R14); they now log its origin, as the sender's own lines did. v1.0.1's text names PushNotificationConfig, which the v1.0.1 proto does not define: the message with `authentication` is TaskPushNotificationConfig (a2a.proto line 469), the name upstream main uses since.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD securely store push notification configurations and credentials
entries.notes: Opt-in, since 2026-10-12: given a PushConfigCipher (with_cipher), the four SQL push-config stores write each config sealed (the whole JSON, so token and authentication.credentials are never stored in the clear) as a2a-sealed:v1:<base64>, bound as associated data to its row (partition, task id, config id), so a sealed config moved to another row does not open; with a cipher an unsealed row is refused unless accept_unsealed_rows, and without one a sealed row is refused. The SDK ships no cipher (tests use AES-256-GCM from ring). Default stores still write plaintext JSON; in-memory stores and Debug output are redacted as before.

entries.requirement: Clients SHOULD use unique, single-purpose tokens for each push notification configuration
entries.notes: Client application choice; SDK neither generates nor checks token uniqueness.

entries.requirement: The Get Extended Agent Card operation MUST require authentication
entries.notes: Refused unless an interceptor reporting authenticates()==true is registered, or the operator opts out with allow_unauthenticated_extended_card(). The check applies to an extended card set with with_extended_agent_card too, with or without a public card on the handler.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST authenticate requests using one of the schemes declared in the public AgentCard.securitySchemes and AgentCard.security fields
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-18 build() asks every authenticating interceptor, through ServerInterceptor::checks_scheme, whether it checks each scheme the public and extended cards declare, and refuses one that checks none of them: a client following the card could never pass it. Bearer and JWT check the HTTP bearer scheme and OAuth 2.0/OIDC (bearer access tokens); ApiKey checks an apiKey scheme in its header (case-insensitive). A custom interceptor that does not answer (None) is not checked; that residual is the integrator's. A card that declares no schemes is not refused (warned nowhere): nothing to compare against.

entries.requirement: Agents MAY return different extended card content based on the authenticated client's identity or authorization level
entries.notes: Since 2026-10-14 an ExtendedCardProvider (RequestHandlerBuilder::with_extended_card_provider) chooses each caller's extended card from the configured one, after the interceptor chain authenticated the request, or refuses the caller. Its card is checked as build() checks the configured one (valid, push notifications only with a push sender, the server's extensions advertised, refused when signed without them). Before: one extended card (with_extended_agent_card) for every authenticated caller.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement appropriate caching headers to control client-side caching of extended cards
entries.notes: GET /extendedAgentCard (RestDispatcher and the axum router) sends Cache-Control: private, no-cache, Vary: Authorization and an ETag over the serialized card, and answers 304 to a matching If-None-Match. JSON-RPC, gRPC and WebSocket fetch the card over POST or a stream, where HTTP caching headers do not apply.

entries.requirement: Extended cards MAY include additional skills not present in the public card
entries.notes: with_extended_agent_card serves a card with skills the public one lacks; the test adds one. Until 2026-10-14 the public and extended card were the same (audit register R56).

entries.requirement: Extended cards MAY expose more detailed capability information (e.g., rate limits, quotas)
entries.notes: The extended card is any valid card the operator sets, capabilities included; build() advertises this server's extensions on it as on the public card. Until 2026-10-14 there was one card.

entries.requirement: Extended cards MAY include organization-specific or user-specific configuration
entries.notes: Organization-specific content in the one extended card (with_extended_agent_card); user-specific content needs per-caller variation, which the handler does not provide (3144).

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD document which capabilities are available at different authentication levels
entries.notes: Operator documentation duty. Re-examined 2026-10-18, kept: what each authentication level unlocks is the agent's policy; the SDK serves the machine-readable form (with_extended_agent_card, ExtendedCardProvider).

entries.requirement: Extended cards SHOULD NOT include sensitive information that could be exploited if leaked (e.g., internal service URLs, unmasked credentials)
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the extended card goes through the same checks as the public one (see §14 3341): an unmasked credential in a URL is refused at build() and by per-caller extended cards, and an internal service URL is reported by card_warnings. Residual, the author's: free text is not inspected.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST validate that clients have appropriate permissions before returning privileged information in extended cards
entries.notes: Re-examined 2026-10-18: the extended card is served only through the interceptor chain and only with an authenticating interceptor (unless allow_unauthenticated_extended_card); ExtendedCardProvider chooses, or refuses, each caller's card. Which permission unlocks what is the agent's policy, expressed in the provider.

entries.requirement: Clients retrieving extended cards SHOULD replace their cached public Agent Card with the extended version for the duration of their authenticated session
entries.notes: The SDK caches a card in two places. A2aClient caches the capabilities it checks calls against (DeclaredCapabilities, from the card it was built from); since 2026-10-13 get_extended_agent_card replaces them with the extended card's (A2aClient::adopt_capabilities), keeping extendedAgentCard declared, and only when the client checks at all. Before, it kept the public card's, so a capability only the extended card declared was refused locally with CapabilityNotDeclared. The other, the resolver's, is replaced when the application calls CachingCardResolver::install_extended_card, which serves the extended card from resolve() until clear_extended_card() or invalidate(); the application decides when the session ends.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD version extended cards appropriately and honor client cache invalidation
entries.notes: card.version stays operator-set. Cache invalidation is honoured through revalidation: no-cache makes the client check every use, and the ETag changes whenever the card does (a new version included, tested), so a stale cached card is replaced on the next request.

entries.requirement: When capabilities.extendedAgentCard is false or not present, the operation MUST return UnsupportedOperationError
entries.notes: Not declared by the handler's card: UnsupportedOperationError. No card on the handler at all and no extended card: UnsupportedOperationError too, since 2026-10-14 (the register's §13.3 row, approved); it answered ExtendedAgentCardNotConfigured, asserting a declaration the handler cannot see. A handler with no public card but an extended card serves it (the card published elsewhere declares the capability).

entries.requirement: When support is declared but no extended card is configured, the operation MUST return ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError
entries.notes: Declared by the handler's card with no with_extended_agent_card: ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError, since 2026-10-14 (audit register R68). Until then this entry was TESTED on the no-card path, the only one that returned -32007; a declared card with no extended card served the public card instead, which this MUST forbids. The test failed before the change.

entries.requirement: Production deployments MUST use encrypted communication (HTTPS for HTTP-based bindings, TLS for gRPC)
entries.notes: Same requirement as §7.1. Every SDK listener can terminate TLS (Server::with_tls for HTTP, WebSocketDispatcher::with_tls since 2026-10-18, GrpcDispatcher::with_tls) and the client reaches https:// and wss:// with verified roots. Using them in production is the deployment's duty, so SUPPORTED. The earlier note (the built-in hyper serve()/WebSocket listeners are plaintext only) was stale for HTTP since Server::with_tls (2026-10-14) and is fixed for WebSocket; serve()/serve_with_addr themselves stay plaintext and run on Server since 2026-10-18, so TLS is Server::bind(..).with_tls(..).

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD use modern TLS configurations (TLS 1.3+ recommended) with strong cipher suites
entries.notes: rustls 0.23.45 implements only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 (its versions.rs defines no other SupportedProtocolVersion), so SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0/1.1 cannot be offered. The client's config negotiates TLS 1.3 with a server that has it and enables only forward-secret AEAD suites (TLS13_* and TLS_ECDHE_*_GCM/CHACHA20_POLY1305); shown to fail with the client limited to TLS 1.2. TLS 1.2 stays enabled for peers without 1.3. The push sender's default config (push/sender.rs) uses the same builder chain; it is read, not handshake-tested.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD enforce HSTS (HTTP Strict Transport Security) headers when using HTTP-based bindings
entries.notes: Opt-in dispatch::Hsts wraps any Dispatcher and sets Strict-Transport-Security on every response, errors included. Browsers ignore HSTS over plain HTTP (RFC 6797 §8.1), so it takes effect on a TLS listener: Server::with_tls (since 2026-10-14) or a TLS terminator in front; axum users add it with their own middleware. Not on by default: a header claiming HTTPS on a plaintext deployment would be wrong. (Until 2026-10-18 this note said the built-in listener is plaintext, which Server::with_tls had made stale.)

entries.requirement: Implementations SHOULD disable support for deprecated SSL/TLS versions (SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1)
entries.notes: rustls 0.23.45 implements only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 (its versions.rs defines no other SupportedProtocolVersion), so SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0/1.1 cannot be offered. The client's config negotiates TLS 1.3 with a server that has it and enables only forward-secret AEAD suites (TLS13_* and TLS_ECDHE_*_GCM/CHACHA20_POLY1305); shown to fail with the client limited to TLS 1.2. TLS 1.2 stays enabled for peers without 1.3. The push sender's default config (push/sender.rs) uses the same builder chain; it is read, not handshake-tested.

entries.requirement: Agents MUST validate all input parameters before processing
entries.notes: Protocol-level validation (ids, metadata size, timestamps, page size clamp, push URL) in the SDK; validation of message content semantics is the executor's. Detailed per-field validation is covered by other sections' audits. A GET's query parameters on the HTTP+JSON binding are validated since 2026-10-13: a historyLength, pageSize, status or includeArtifacts that does not parse is InvalidParams (400) on RestDispatcher and A2aRouter alike, where it was read as absent.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement appropriate limits on message sizes, file sizes, and request complexity
entries.notes: Body cap (4 MiB default), gRPC message cap, WS frame cap, metadata/id/parts/artifacts caps. A body not received within body_read_timeout is 408 on HTTP+JSON (the axum router's answer too) since 2026-10-13; every body read failure was 413 there, a stalled upload included. A body stream hyper cannot read is 400. JSON-RPC answers either with -32700.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD sanitize or validate file content types and reject unexpected media types
entries.notes: Part mediaType checked against card defaultInputModes/skill inputModes; parts without mediaType and content sniffing are not checked (content sanitization is the executor's).

entries.requirement: API keys, tokens, and other credentials MUST be treated as secrets
entries.notes: Constant-time comparison, Debug shows counts not keys, identity labels separate from credentials, push secrets redacted. Exception: SQL push-config stores keep credentials plaintext at rest (see 3131). Client: until 2026-10-14 (audit register R17) the derived Debug of ClientRequest, ClientResponse, CardFetchOptions and WebSocketTransportConfig printed header values (the Authorization an auth interceptor adds) and push-config params and results verbatim; they print header names and JSON keys now, never values.

entries.requirement: Credentials SHOULD be rotated periodically
entries.notes: JWKS remote key sets support key rotation; client token providers refresh. Static allow-lists are fixed at construction.

entries.requirement: Credentials SHOULD be transmitted only over encrypted connections
entries.notes: Neither client auth interceptors nor the push sender refuse to send credentials over http://; deployment choice.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement credential revocation mechanisms
entries.notes: No revocation API (no jti/deny-list in jwt.rs; static key/token lists immutable after construction); revocation via JWKS key removal/expiry or a custom interceptor.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD log authentication failures
entries.notes: With the `audit` feature + with_audit, refused calls are recorded (test sends a credential-less call and asserts a record with no actor). The auth interceptors themselves emit no log line; metrics on_error counts failures.

entries.requirement: Agents SHOULD implement rate limiting to prevent brute-force attacks

The peer is CallContext::peer_addr, which every binding but SLIMRPC records when the SDK serves it (axum: with ConnectInfo or a PeerAddr extension), or the client address trusted x-forwarded-for hops name; SLIMRPC records no peer, and since 2026-10-14 drops a caller's x-forwarded-for, x-real-ip and forwarded (audit register R41), which with trusted hops let a caller pick its own key, so an unidentified SLIMRPC caller is not throttled until the binding records a verified peer (R13); at most max_peers are tracked, failing open beyond. A default server throttles nothing. RateLimitInterceptor limits throughput per caller and does not use the peer address.
